Smith, pilot, both assigned to Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron (VMGR) 352, Marine Aircraft Group 11, 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing, walk toward a KC-130J Super Hercules during the Marine Air Ground Task Force demonstration of the 2026 Marine Corps Air Station Miramar Air Show in San Diego, Sept. 25, 2026. The MAGTF Demo displays the coordinated use of close-air support, armor, artillery and infantry forces and
items.body:
Midgette, left, a co-pilot and Capt.

Smith, pilot, both assigned to Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron (VMGR) 352, Marine Aircraft Group 11, 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing, walk toward a KC-130J Super Hercules during the Marine Air Ground Task Force demonstration of the 2026 Marine Corps Air Station Miramar Air Show in San Diego, Sept.

The MAGTF Demo displays the coordinated use of close-air support, armor, artillery and infantry forces and provides a visual representation of how the Marine Corps operates.

America's Air Show 2026 is a unique and incredible opportunity to witness Marine and joint aviation capabilities, civilian performers and the world-famous Blue Angels; to celebrate America’s 250th birthday alongside Marines and to see first-hand the innovative spirit of the Marine Corps through emerging technologies and forward-thinking.

Marine Corps photo by Lance Cpl.
zhParas: 左为副驾驶米吉特（Midgette），以及 Capt.
史密斯（Smith），飞行员，两人均隶属于海军陆战队第3航空联队第11航空大队海军陆战队空中加油运输中队（VMGR）352，在2026年9月于圣迭戈举行的海军陆战队米拉马尔航空站航空展的海军陆战队空地特遣部队演示期间，走向一架 KC-130J Super Hercules。
MAGTF 演示展示了近距离空中支援、装甲、炮兵和步兵部队的协同运用，并直观呈现了海军陆战队的运作方式。
2026年美国航空展是一次独特而难得的机会，可见证海军陆战队和联合航空能力、民间表演者以及世界闻名的“蓝天使”飞行表演队；与海军陆战队员一同庆祝美国250周年诞辰，并通过新兴技术和前瞻性思维亲身领略海军陆战队的创新精神。
海军陆战队照片，拍摄者：Lance Cpl.

items.title: Air Force Certifies Anduril Barracuda Cruise Missile for Open System Updates
items.author: Todd South
items.summary: The Anduril-built Barracuda cruise missile recently received certification as the Air Force’s first large-scale production munition compliant with open systems architecture. The post Air Force Certifies Anduril Barracuda Cruise Missile for Open System Updates appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
The Anduril-built Barracuda cruise missile recently received certification as the Air Force’s first large-scale production munition compliant with open systems architecture.

The certification clears the way for the new weapon, billed as a way for commanders to carry multiple tools in their belts, with options to swap payloads and other features once the missile is delivered to the Air Force.

“Barracuda’s open software architecture means that it can be equipped with a variety of different datalinks and communications modalities, unlocking integrations with a vast spectrum of different aircraft and other communications nodes,” an Anduril spokesperson told Air & Space Forces Magazine Sept. 25.

Anduril is slated to deliver its first Barracuda missiles to the Pentagon in early 2027.

The Air Force Research Laboratory’s Munition Open Architecture Test and Evaluation Laboratory, or MOATEL, oversees the Weapon Open System Architecture certification process. The lab’s engineers spent four days at Anduril’s California headquarters verifying compliance with open system architecture, known as WOSA, on Anduril hardware, an Anduril spokesperson said.

“This is showing that open architecture can scale beyond prototypes,” Jonathan Shaver, program manager and creator of WOSA at AFRL’s Air Warfare Directorate, said in an Anduril release. “Without that independent path from S&T to MOATEL, the industrial base cannot deliver new technology to the warfighter at the speed the fight requires.”

The certified modularity option for the cruise missile could give commanders a plethora of features to work with in the planned-for stockpile boost.

The Pentagon announced multi-year framework agreements for its Family of Affordable Mass Missiles program in July. Anduril, CoAspire, and Zone 5 Technologies were selected. The agreements call for the three companies to produce 8,000 missiles annually once production ramps up. That timeline targets 5,300 missiles in 2028, rising to 8,000 by 2031.

The MOATEL verification tested 14 WOSA domains: Mission Autonomy, Seeker, Inertial Measurement Unit, GPS, Air-Data Sensor, Propulsion, Airframe Control, Target State Estimator, Altimeter Aiding Navigation, Clock, Autopilot, Guidance, Navigation, and Munitions Data Bus.

“It’s easy to talk about modularity and open architectures in the abstract. Proving it through an independent assessment is harder,” Pat Morris, vice president of advanced effects at Anduril, said in the release.

With the MOATEL assessment, those munitions can be updated and upgraded as users need new technology or as mission requirements change.

Modular Munitions Options

Anduril has integrated four different turbojet engines into the Barracuda 500, giving the company flexibility in providing engines as it seeks to churn out missiles in the coming years.

The MOATEL assessment’s certification of the open-architecture software also clears the way to use the Barracuda with current and future communication systems.

So far, the company has built three base model Barracudas: the Barracuda 100, with a roughly 35-pound payload and a range of more than 120 nautical miles; the Barracuda 250, also with a 35-pound payload and a range of more than 200 nautical miles; and the Barracuda 500, with a greater than 100-pound payload and more than 500 nautical miles of range. The company spokesperson said the WOSA verification applies across the Barracuda variants.

During AFA’s Air, Space & Cyber conference last week, Lockheed Martin announced its new AGM-158 FLEX. The munitions provide modularity, including swappable nose and launch options for the precision-guided Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile, known as the JASSM, and its companion Long-Range Anti-Ship Missile, or LRASM.

The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center at Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, posted a notice to industry seeking modular parts for its Extended Range Attack Munition in January 2025, signaling a push toward broader munitions options for the stockpile that the service and other branches are now building.
zhParas: 由Anduril公司制造的Barracuda巡航导弹近日获得认证，成为美国空军首款符合开放系统架构的大规模生产弹药。
该认证为这款新武器扫清了道路。它被宣传为一种让指挥官“腰带上多揣几件工具”的手段——导弹交付空军后，还可选择更换有效载荷及其他功能配置。
Anduril公司发言人9月25日对《空军与太空军杂志》表示：“Barracuda的开放软件架构意味着它可以配备多种不同的数据链和通信方式，从而能够与种类繁多的各类飞机及其他通信节点实现集成。”
Anduril公司计划于2027年初向五角大楼交付首批Barracuda导弹。
美国空军研究实验室下属的弹药开放架构测试与评估实验室（MOATEL）负责监督武器开放系统架构的认证流程。Anduril公司发言人称，该实验室的工程师在Anduril位于加利福尼亚州的总部驻留四天，对Anduril硬件进行了核查，确认其符合被称为WOSA的开放系统架构要求。
美国空军研究实验室空战局WOSA项目经理兼创建者乔纳森·谢弗（Jonathan Shaver）在Anduril发布的一则消息中表示：“这表明开放架构能够超越原型阶段实现规模化。如果没有从科技部门到MOATEL的这条独立路径，工业基础就无法以作战所需的速度向作战人员交付新技术。”
在计划中的库存扩充中，这款巡航导弹获得认证的模块化选项可为指挥官提供众多可供使用的功能。
五角大楼于7月宣布了其“经济型大规模导弹系列”（Family of Affordable Mass Missiles）计划的多年框架协议。Anduril、CoAspire和Zone 5 Technologies三家公司入选。协议要求这三家公司在产能提升后每年生产8000枚导弹。该时间表的目标是2028年达到5300枚，到2031年增至8000枚。
MOATEL 验证测试了 14 个 WOSA 域：任务自主、导引头、惯性测量单元、GPS、大气数据传感器、推进、机体控制、目标状态估计器、高度表辅助导航、时钟、自动驾驶仪、制导、导航和弹药数据总线。
“抽象地谈论模块化和开放架构很容易。通过独立评估来证明它则更难，”安杜里尔公司先进效应副总裁帕特·莫里斯（Pat Morris）在新闻稿中表示。
借助 MOATEL 评估，这些弹药可以在用户需要新技术或任务要求变化时进行更新和升级。
模块化弹药选项
安杜里尔已将四种不同的涡喷发动机集成到 Barracuda 500 中，这使该公司在寻求未来几年大量生产导弹时，在发动机供应方面拥有灵活性。
MOATEL 评估对开放架构软件的认证，也为将 Barracuda 与当前及未来的通信系统配合使用扫清了道路。

截至目前，该公司已制造了三种基础型号的 Barracuda：Barracuda 100，有效载荷约 35-pound，射程超过 120 nautical miles；Barracuda 250，同样具有 35-pound 的有效载荷，射程超过 200 nautical miles；以及 Barracuda 500，有效载荷超过 100-pound，射程超过 500 nautical miles。公司发言人表示，WOSA 验证适用于所有 Barracuda 变体。
上周，在 AFA 的 Air, Space & Cyber 会议上，洛克希德·马丁公司宣布了其新型 AGM-158 FLEX。这些弹药具备模块化特性，包括可为精确制导的联合空面防区外导弹（JASSM）及其配套的远程反舰导弹（LRASM）提供可更换的头部和发射选项。
佛罗里达州埃格林空军基地的美国空军寿命周期管理中心于2025年1月向工业界发布通告，为其增程攻击弹药寻求模块化部件，表明空军正推动为空军及其他军种目前正在建立的库存提供更广泛的弹药选项。

items.title: Air Force Injects $87M into IVEWS F-16 Electronic Warfare Upgrades
items.author: Todd South
items.summary: The Air Force has invested $87.4 million to upgrade the F-16 Fighting Falcon's electronic warfare capabilities, bolstering the fighter's self-protection against increasingly advanced threats. Bringing the total program value to $1.92 billion, the move is expected to jump-start fielding by funding low-rate initial production of the AN/ALQ-257 Integrated Viper Electronic Warfare Suite, or IVEWS. The post Air Force Injects $87M into IVEWS F-16 Electronic Warfare Upgrades appeared first on <
items.body:
The Air Force has invested $87.4 million to upgrade the F-16 Fighting Falcon’s electronic warfare capabilities, bolstering the fighter’s self-protection against increasingly advanced threats.

Bringing the total program value to $1.92 billion, the move is expected to jump-start fielding by funding low-rate initial production of the AN/ALQ-257 Integrated Viper Electronic Warfare Suite, or IVEWS, which is integrated into the fighter’s airframe.

This money is intended to produce an upgraded Viper for use in the Middle East, as part of an effort pushed by the U.S. military’s Central Command.

Work on the low-rate initial production batch at the company’s Illinois facility is expected to conclude by the end of 2029. The Air Force Lifecycle Management Center, Wright-Patterson, Ohio, oversees the contract.

The company says the new EW system is sorely needed for the F-16’s future fights.

“You cannot defeat what you cannot see,” said Shalini Gupta, vice president of electronic warfare and targeting at Northrop Grumman, in a statement to Air & Space Forces Magazine. “A modern EW suite is essential for operations in contested airspace. We are producing fully functional, flight-proven systems now. From day one, our customers gain the ability to geolocate threats with a single aircraft, and the confidence that comes with having a U.S. program of record system on board.”

The F-16 has seen a lot of action in Operation Epic Fury, and while its existing capabilities have handled Iranian air defenses and electronic warfare capabilities, peer adversaries such as the Chinese military have more sophisticated means to foil the jet fighter’s aims.

The Air Force issued an urgent operational need statement in September 2025 that triggered a congressionally supplied $187 million in its fiscal 2026 reconciliation bill, which sped up system qualification and flight testing.

After CENTCOM’s operational need statement, Northrop and the Air Force made the effort a priority.

“This is one of many efforts to keep our fourth-gen platforms competitive as the adversary advances,” Lt. Gen. Derek France, then-commander of Air Forces Central, said in September 2025 about IVEWS. “That’s the bumper sticker, if you will.”

The recently announced additional $87.4 million LRIP modification fuels the initial production of the Viper suites. Full-rate production of the suites for the full 450-aircraft fleet is scheduled to follow this initial batch.

The initial production tranche for the Air Force was to outfit 72 Block 50 F-16s with IVEWS, with more likely to arrive as production ramps up, the company’s vice president of targeting and survivability Jim Conroy told Air & Space Forces Magazine in a 2025 interview.

Iran operates radar-guided and electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) air defense systems. Non-traditional Houthi air defense systems proved a particular challenge for U.S. aircraft, including F-16s, during last year’s Operation Rough Rider against the Houthis in Yemen.

During Operation Epic Fury, the Air Force used its Block 50 F-16s in a suppression of enemy air defenses role, U.S. officials have said, and deployed most of its Wild Weasel SEAD F-16 units to support operations against Iran. Those units’ F-16s can carry AGM-88 anti-radiation missiles and are equipped with HARM Targeting System, or HTS, pods—a capability the Air Force’s other fourth-generation fighter, the F-15E Strike Eagle, lacks.

IVEWS is an ultra-wideband, sophisticated EW system capable of radar warning, active jamming, and detecting, identifying, and locating threats, suited for fifth- and sixth-generation aircraft.

It can also conduct single-aircraft autonomous geolocation, meaning one aircraft can find an enemy radar and map a threat while actively using the aircraft’s jammer. Older systems required multiple aircraft to triangulate a radar location and required pilots to shut off jammers when mapping threats.

Under the USAF “Big Iron” software compliance standard, teams will be able to quickly update IVEWS system software files without hardware modifications or grounding the aircraft for days, weeks, or months.

IVEWS began flight tests in 2024 and has undergone more than 550 hours of effective testing across 300 sorties during operational assessments, Northrop Vice President for Mission Systems Mike Minahan said in a July call with reporters.

The system works in conjunction with the AN/AG-83 Scalable Agile Beam Radar. The radar uses an Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) to enable faster target tracking.

As of mid-May, Northrop had delivered 1,000 SABR radars to its F-16 customers. The new radar uses digital tracking as opposed to the legacy AN/APG-66 and AN-APG-68 radars that it is replacing.

IVEWS, the SABR, and the upgraded LITENING LA pod, which gives the aircraft a 50 percent increase in the range of its targeting system, are crucial to keeping the aging F-16 combat-worthy. The pod is also used on the F-15E Strike Eagle, A-10 Thunderbolt II, B-52 Stratofortress, and the Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet.

IVEWS would likely be equipped on possible future Air Force new-build “F-16G” purchases the service will consider, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported.

The LITENING LA, an upgrade from the current LITENING pod, entered flight testing in December, according to Northrop officials.
zhParas: 美国空军已投资8740万美元，用于升级F-16 Fighting Falcon的电子战能力，以增强这款战斗机对日益先进威胁的自卫能力。
此举使项目总价值达到19.2亿美元，预计将通过资助 AN/ALQ-257 Integrated Viper Electronic Warfare Suite（简称 IVEWS）的低速初始生产来启动列装，该系统集成于该战斗机机体。
这笔资金旨在生产供中东使用的升级版 Viper，这是美军中央司令部推动的一项行动的一部分。
该公司伊利诺伊州工厂的低速初始生产批次工作预计将于2029年底前结束。位于俄亥俄州赖特-帕特森的空军生命周期管理中心负责监督该合同。
该公司表示，F-16未来的战斗迫切需要这种新型电子战系统。

“你无法击败你看不见的目标，”诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司电子战与目标定位副总裁沙利尼·古普塔（Shalini Gupta）在给《Air & Space Forces Magazine》的声明中说。“现代电子战套件对于在争夺激烈的空域中作战至关重要。我们现在正在生产功能完备、经过飞行验证的系统。从第一天起，我们的客户就能获得用单架飞机对威胁进行地理定位的能力，以及机上拥有美国正式采办项目系统所带来的信心。”
F-16在“史诗之怒”行动中经历了大量实战，虽然其现有能力已能应对伊朗的防空和电子战能力，但中国军队等同等对手拥有更先进的手段来挫败这款战斗机的目标。
美国空军于2025年9月发布了一份紧急作战需求声明，这促使国会在其2026财年预算和解法案中提供1.87亿美元，从而加快了系统鉴定和飞行测试。
在美军中央司令部发布作战需求声明后，诺斯罗普和美国空军将这项工作列为优先事项。
“这是随着对手不断进步，为保持我们四代平台竞争力而采取的众多努力之一，”时任美国空军中央司令部司令的 Lt. Gen. 德里克·弗朗斯（Derek France）在2025年9月谈到IVEWS时表示。“如果愿意这么说，这就是那句口号。”
最近宣布的额外8740万美元LRIP修改资金，推动了Viper套件的初始生产。针对全部450架飞机机队的该套件全速生产，计划在这批初始产品之后展开。
美国空军的初始生产批次计划为72架 Block 50 F-16 装备 IVEWS；该公司负责瞄准与生存能力的副总裁吉姆·康罗伊（Jim Conroy）在2025年接受《Air & Space Forces Magazine》采访时表示，随着生产提速，可能会有更多飞机加装该系统。
伊朗装备有雷达制导和光电/红外（EO/IR）防空系统。在去年于也门针对胡塞武装的“Rough Rider”行动期间，非传统胡塞防空系统被证明对包括F-16在内的美国飞机构成特别挑战。
美国官员表示，在“Epic Fury”行动期间，美国空军将其 Block 50 F-16 用于压制敌方防空任务，并部署了其大部分“野鼬鼠”SEAD F-16部队，以支援针对伊朗的行动。这些部队的F-16可携带AGM-88反辐射导弹，并装备HARM瞄准系统（HTS）吊舱——这是美国空军另一款四代战斗机F-15E Strike Eagle所不具备的能力。
IVEWS是一种超宽带、先进的电子战系统，具备雷达告警、主动干扰以及探测、识别和定位威胁的能力，适用于第五代和第六代飞机。
它还可以进行单机自主地理定位，这意味着，一架飞机可以在主动使用本机干扰器的同时，发现敌方雷达并标定威胁。较旧系统需要多架飞机对雷达位置进行三角定位，并要求飞行员在测绘威胁时关闭干扰器。
根据美国空军“Big Iron”软件合规标准，团队将能够快速更新 IVEWS 系统软件文件，而无需修改硬件，也无需让飞机停飞数天、数周或数月。
IVEWS 于 2024 年开始飞行测试，在作战评估期间已通过 300 架次、超过 550 小时的有效测试，诺斯罗普公司负责任务系统的副总裁迈克·米纳汉 (Mike Minahan) 在 7 月与记者的通话中表示。
该系统与 AN/AG-83 Scalable Agile Beam Radar 协同工作。该雷达采用有源电子扫描阵列 (AESA)，可实现更快的目标跟踪。
截至 5 月中旬，诺斯罗普已向 F-16 客户交付了 1,000 部 SABR 雷达。新雷达采用数字跟踪，不同于其正在替换的老式 AN/APG-66 和 AN/APG-68 雷达。
IVEWS、SABR 和升级后的 LITENING LA 吊舱（使该机瞄准系统的作用距离增加 50%）对于让老化的 F-16 保持作战能力至关重要。该吊舱还用于 F-15E Strike Eagle、A-10 Thunderbolt II、B-52 Stratofortress 以及美国海军 F/A-18 Super Hornet。
据《空军与太空军杂志》报道，IVEWS 很可能会装备在美国空军未来可能考虑采购的新造“F-16G”上。
据诺斯罗普公司官员称，LITENING LA 是当前 LITENING 吊舱的升级版，已于 12 月进入飞行测试。

美国空军于2025年9月发布了一份紧急作战需求声明，这促使国会在其2026财年预算和解法案中提供1.87亿美元，从而加快了系统鉴定和飞行测试。

在美军中央司令部发布作战需求声明后，诺斯罗普和美国空军将这项工作列为优先事项。

“这是随着对手不断进步，为保持我们四代平台竞争力而采取的众多努力之一，”时任美国空军中央司令部司令的 Lt. Gen. 德里克·弗朗斯（Derek France）在2025年9月谈到IVEWS时表示。“如果愿意这么说，这就是那句口号。”

最近宣布的额外8740万美元LRIP修改资金，推动了Viper套件的初始生产。针对全部450架飞机机队的该套件全速生产，计划在这批初始产品之后展开。

美国空军的初始生产批次计划为72架 Block 50 F-16 装备 IVEWS；该公司负责瞄准与生存能力的副总裁吉姆·康罗伊（Jim Conroy）在2025年接受《Air & Space Forces Magazine》采访时表示，随着生产提速，可能会有更多飞机加装该系统。

伊朗装备有雷达制导和光电/红外（EO/IR）防空系统。在去年于也门针对胡塞武装的“Rough Rider”行动期间，非传统胡塞防空系统被证明对包括F-16在内的美国飞机构成特别挑战。

美国官员表示，在“Epic Fury”行动期间，美国空军将其 Block 50 F-16 用于压制敌方防空任务，并部署了其大部分“野鼬鼠”SEAD F-16部队，以支援针对伊朗的行动。这些部队的F-16可携带AGM-88反辐射导弹，并装备HARM瞄准系统（HTS）吊舱——这是美国空军另一款四代战斗机F-15E Strike Eagle所不具备的能力。

IVEWS是一种超宽带、先进的电子战系统，具备雷达告警、主动干扰以及探测、识别和定位威胁的能力，适用于第五代和第六代飞机。

它还可以进行单机自主地理定位，这意味着，一架飞机可以在主动使用本机干扰器的同时，发现敌方雷达并标定威胁。较旧系统需要多架飞机对雷达位置进行三角定位，并要求飞行员在测绘威胁时关闭干扰器。

根据美国空军“Big Iron”软件合规标准，团队将能够快速更新 IVEWS 系统软件文件，而无需修改硬件，也无需让飞机停飞数天、数周或数月。

IVEWS 于 2024 年开始飞行测试，在作战评估期间已通过 300 架次、超过 550 小时的有效测试，诺斯罗普公司负责任务系统的副总裁迈克·米纳汉 (Mike Minahan) 在 7 月与记者的通话中表示。

该系统与 AN/AG-83 Scalable Agile Beam Radar 协同工作。该雷达采用有源电子扫描阵列 (AESA)，可实现更快的目标跟踪。

截至 5 月中旬，诺斯罗普已向 F-16 客户交付了 1,000 部 SABR 雷达。新雷达采用数字跟踪，不同于其正在替换的老式 AN/APG-66 和 AN/APG-68 雷达。

IVEWS、SABR 和升级后的 LITENING LA 吊舱（使该机瞄准系统的作用距离增加 50%）对于让老化的 F-16 保持作战能力至关重要。该吊舱还用于 F-15E Strike Eagle、A-10 Thunderbolt II、B-52 Stratofortress 以及美国海军 F/A-18 Super Hornet。

据《空军与太空军杂志》报道，IVEWS 很可能会装备在美国空军未来可能考虑采购的新造“F-16G”上。

据诺斯罗普公司官员称，LITENING LA 是当前 LITENING 吊舱的升级版，已于 12 月进入飞行测试。

Special Operations Command Para-Commandos conduct a parachute demonstration at the 2026 Marine Corps Air Station Miramar Air Show in San Diego, Sept.

The Para-Commandos are the USSOCOM's premier aerial parachute demonstration team, performing at public events across the nation to inform the public about the USSOCOM.

items.title: 144th Medical Company (Area Support) Departure Ceremony
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: On Sept. 20, 2026, Soldiers of the Utah Army National Guard’s 144th Medical Company (Area Support) departed from Roland R. Wright Air National Guard Base in Draper, Utah, beginning a deployment to Europe. Family and friends gathered to say goodbye as unit leaders recognized both the Soldiers’ commitment and the support of those staying home.
items.body:
DRAPER, UT – Inside a 1960s-era hangar at Roland R. Wright, Soldiers of the 144th Medical Company (Area Support) held their families and friends close one more time. On Sept. 20, 2026, the hangar’s large silver doors screeched open as final embraces, quiet farewells and last moments together gave way to departure. After months of preparation, the ceremony marked the beginning of the unit’s deployment and a new chapter for the Soldiers, families and friends gathered to see them off.

Utah Army National Guard Assistant Adjutant Gen. Col. Andrew Owens stated, the 144th “carry with them the legacy of absolute, unyielding commitment. Anchored by a model that defines their spirit and unit motto, ‘burn the ships’. Drawing from Hernán Cortés’ legendary resolve in 1519, where he destroyed his fleet to destroy any psychological option to retreat.” As they burn their metaphorical ships, they destroy with them any chance of giving up, any option of retreat, from healing and saving the lives of their fellow service members.

In the same way that the Soldiers would be critical to those they care for, the leadership wanted to recognize those who play the same role in the lives of the Soldiers deploying. Their remarks recognized the months of preparation leading up to the departure and the important role families and friends play as Soldiers transition from preparation to deployment. Col. Patricia Brown, commander of the 97th Troop Command, addressed those gathered and offered her appreciation to the families and friends of the deploying Soldiers.

“Our mission is unique in that we get to positively impact our fellow Soldiers to keep them healthy and in the fight,” stated Maj. Dan Boyden, the commander of the 144th. “Our efforts directly affect all other missions because medical readiness is the key to operational readiness.”

The 144th will arrive in Texas to complete their premobilization training before deploying. The mobilization will support United States and NATO efforts in Europe to provide role II care. Role II care includes collection and evacuation of patients, medical treatment, and short-term patient hold. Ancillary medical care will include dental, behavioral health, laboratory services, and X-ray, as well as supporting medical care, clinical needs, and medical readiness for deployed troops in the area.

The medical capabilities of the role II and the service and sacrifice of the Soldiers selected for this deployment will allow U.S. service members to maintain mission readiness and capabilities through supporting NATO as a critical medical facility.

Every Soldier and family will experience a transition throughout the course of this deployment, and with that transition will come its own unique set of challenges. There will be good days that bring moments of pride, connection, and reassurance, as well as difficult days that test patience, resilience, and strength. While every deployment looks different, each one represents a period of change, growth, and perseverance for both the Soldier and those waiting for them at home.

During the ceremony, Brig. Gen. Michael Kjar gave his personal support to the family members of Soldiers who would be staying behind. “Something’s going to break in your home; you’re going to need somebody; call me; if I can’t get there, I’ll get somebody there.”

With the Soldiers lined up at the aircraft steps, waves and farewells stretched across the flight line. One by one, members of the 144th MCAS boarded the aircraft as their families and friends watched from behind. When the last Soldier stepped inside, the door closed and the aircraft began to move. Those gathered remained in place, watching as it taxied away, the final moments of goodbye giving way to the deployment ahead.
zhParas: 犹他州德雷珀——在Roland R. Wright一处建于20世纪60年代的机库内，第144医疗连（区域支援）的士兵们再次与家人和朋友紧紧相拥。2026年9月20日，机库巨大的银色大门嘎吱作响地打开，最后的拥抱、无声的告别和共处的最后时光让位于启程。经过数月准备，这场仪式标志着该部队部署的开始，也标志着前来送行的士兵、家人和朋友开启了新的篇章。

犹他州陆军国民警卫队助理副官长 Col. 安德鲁·欧文斯（Andrew Owens）表示，第144医疗连“承载着绝对、不屈不挠的奉献精神的传承。支撑他们的是诠释其精神与部队座右铭‘焚舟’的典范——源自埃尔南·科尔特斯（Hernán Cortés）1519年的传奇决心，他摧毁自己的舰队，以断绝一切心理上的退路。”当他们焚毁象征意义上的船只时，也一并断绝了任何放弃的可能、任何撤退的选项，只为救治和挽救战友的生命。
正如这些士兵对他们所照料的人至关重要一样，领导层也希望表彰那些在即将部署的士兵生活中扮演同样角色的人。他们的讲话肯定了出发前数月的准备，以及家人和朋友在士兵从准备转向部署过程中所发挥的重要作用。第97部队司令部司令 Col. 帕特里夏·布朗（Patricia Brown）向在场人员讲话，并对即将部署士兵的家人和朋友表示感谢。
“我们的任务之所以独特，在于我们能够积极影响战友，让他们保持健康、继续战斗，”第144医疗连指挥官 Maj. 丹·博伊登（Dan Boyden）表示。“我们的努力直接影响所有其他任务，因为医疗战备是作战战备的关键。”
第144医疗连将抵达得克萨斯州，完成动员前训练后再行部署。此次动员将支持美国及北约在欧洲提供二级医疗救治的行动。二级医疗救治包括伤病员的收治与后送、医疗救治以及伤病员短期留治。辅助医疗护理将包括牙科、行为健康、检验服务和X光，并为该地区部署部队的医疗护理、临床需求和医疗战备提供支持。
二级医疗救治的医疗能力，以及被选中参加此次部署的士兵的服役与牺牲，将使美国军人能够通过作为关键医疗设施支持北约，保持任务战备与能力。
在此次部署全过程中，每名士兵和每个家庭都将经历一段转变，而伴随这种转变而来的，是一系列各自独特的挑战。会有带来自豪、联结与慰藉时刻的好日子，也会有考验耐心、韧性与力量的艰难日子。尽管每次部署看起来各不相同，但每一次对士兵和在家等待他们的人来说，都代表着一段变化、成长与坚持的时期。
仪式期间，Brig. Gen. 迈克尔·基亚尔（Michael Kjar）向将留在后方的士兵家属表达了个人支持。“你家里总会有什么东西坏掉；你会需要有人帮忙；给我打电话；如果我去不了，我会找人过去。”
士兵们在飞机舷梯旁列队，挥手与告别在停机坪上此起彼伏。144th MCAS 的成员一个接一个登机，家人和朋友在身后注视着。当最后一名士兵步入机舱，舱门关闭，飞机开始移动。送行的人群留在原地，目送飞机滑行离去，告别的最后时刻让位于即将展开的部署。

犹他州德雷珀——在Roland R. Wright一处建于20世纪60年代的机库内，第144医疗连（区域支援）的士兵们再次与家人和朋友紧紧相拥。2026年9月20日，机库巨大的银色大门嘎吱作响地打开，最后的拥抱、无声的告别和共处的最后时光让位于启程。经过数月准备，这场仪式标志着该部队部署的开始，也标志着前来送行的士兵、家人和朋友开启了新的篇章。

犹他州陆军国民警卫队助理副官长 Col. 安德鲁·欧文斯（Andrew Owens）表示，第144医疗连“承载着绝对、不屈不挠的奉献精神的传承。支撑他们的是诠释其精神与部队座右铭‘焚舟’的典范——源自埃尔南·科尔特斯（Hernán Cortés）1519年的传奇决心，他摧毁自己的舰队，以断绝一切心理上的退路。”当他们焚毁象征意义上的船只时，也一并断绝了任何放弃的可能、任何撤退的选项，只为救治和挽救战友的生命。

正如这些士兵对他们所照料的人至关重要一样，领导层也希望表彰那些在即将部署的士兵生活中扮演同样角色的人。他们的讲话肯定了出发前数月的准备，以及家人和朋友在士兵从准备转向部署过程中所发挥的重要作用。第97部队司令部司令 Col. 帕特里夏·布朗（Patricia Brown）向在场人员讲话，并对即将部署士兵的家人和朋友表示感谢。

“我们的任务之所以独特，在于我们能够积极影响战友，让他们保持健康、继续战斗，”第144医疗连指挥官 Maj. 丹·博伊登（Dan Boyden）表示。“我们的努力直接影响所有其他任务，因为医疗战备是作战战备的关键。”

第144医疗连将抵达得克萨斯州，完成动员前训练后再行部署。此次动员将支持美国及北约在欧洲提供二级医疗救治的行动。二级医疗救治包括伤病员的收治与后送、医疗救治以及伤病员短期留治。辅助医疗护理将包括牙科、行为健康、检验服务和X光，并为该地区部署部队的医疗护理、临床需求和医疗战备提供支持。

二级医疗救治的医疗能力，以及被选中参加此次部署的士兵的服役与牺牲，将使美国军人能够通过作为关键医疗设施支持北约，保持任务战备与能力。

在此次部署全过程中，每名士兵和每个家庭都将经历一段转变，而伴随这种转变而来的，是一系列各自独特的挑战。会有带来自豪、联结与慰藉时刻的好日子，也会有考验耐心、韧性与力量的艰难日子。尽管每次部署看起来各不相同，但每一次对士兵和在家等待他们的人来说，都代表着一段变化、成长与坚持的时期。

仪式期间，Brig. Gen. 迈克尔·基亚尔（Michael Kjar）向将留在后方的士兵家属表达了个人支持。“你家里总会有什么东西坏掉；你会需要有人帮忙；给我打电话；如果我去不了，我会找人过去。”

士兵们在飞机舷梯旁列队，挥手与告别在停机坪上此起彼伏。144th MCAS 的成员一个接一个登机，家人和朋友在身后注视着。当最后一名士兵步入机舱，舱门关闭，飞机开始移动。送行的人群留在原地，目送飞机滑行离去，告别的最后时刻让位于即将展开的部署。

items.title: Ukraine’s deadly AI training platform for drone tech opens to UK companies
items.author: Katie Livingstone
items.summary: Ukraine opens wartime battlefield data to Britain through Avengers AI Labs, giving British companies access to data for AI drone development.
items.body:
KYIV, Ukraine — The British Ministry of Defence has struck a partnership with Ukraine’s Avengers AI Labs, an information-rich platform built to train AI for battlefield drones, marking the first time that Kyiv has opened up its trove of wartime data to an outside government, according to officials in London.

The announcement comes a month after U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham signed an AI deal with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy while visiting Kyiv alongside other allies to honor Ukraine’s independence day and pledge continued support to the war-torn nation.

“Ukraine is the frontline of freedom for us all. On my recent visit to Kyiv, I saw first-hand the courage and resilience of the Ukrainian people,” U.K. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a statement on Friday.

“I also saw the extraordinary innovation which is allowing them to repel Putin’s illegal and unprovoked invasion.”

“This world-first access to real battlefield data will allow British companies to continue pushing the frontier of defence innovation, deterring our enemies and making us safer at home as well as further strengthening Ukraine,” Streeting said.

Ukraine has shared its combat-derived AI training data with allies in the past, but this is the first time that Kyiv has granted a foreign country access to the machine-learning infrastructure driving its rapid AI innovations seen across the front.

Avengers AI Labs holds an annotated dataset of more than 5 million battlefield frames, plus sensor data covering millions of object detections — including tanks, artillery, air defense, infantry, Shahed drones, reconnaissance UAVs, and more) — built mainly from Ukraine’s DELTA battle-management system, according to a release by Ukrainian officials.

Data is anonymized and released on a delay to avoid endangering personnel still fighting, according to Ukraine’s Defence Ministry. U.K. companies also work inside a secure perimeter that doesn’t allow them to download the underlying dataset, according to Ukraine’s MOD.

The British defense ministry is now inviting up to a dozen companies to submit proposals for how they would use the platform, especially to develop tech that would enable full functionality even when communications are degraded or satellite navigation is unavailable.

“It is exactly the kind of practical partnership the Taskforce was set up to drive, supporting our ally Ukraine while strengthening sovereign capability here in Britain,” U.K. AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said in Friday’s statement.

Katie Livingstone is the Ukraine correspondent for Defense News and Military Times. Based in Kyiv, she has covered Russia's full-scale invasion since its first days. She is a former Fulbright fellow whose award-winning work has appeared in outlets across Europe and the U.S.
zhParas: 基辅，乌克兰——据伦敦官员称，英国国防部已与乌克兰的 Avengers AI Labs 建立合作关系，该实验室是一个信息丰富的平台，旨在为战场无人机训练人工智能，这标志着基辅首次向外国政府开放其战时数据宝库。
这一消息宣布的一个月前，英国首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）在访问基辅期间与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基（Volodymyr Zelenskyy）签署了一项人工智能协议，当时他与其他盟友一道前往基辅，纪念乌克兰独立日，并承诺继续支持这个饱受战争蹂躏的国家。
英国国防大臣韦斯·斯特里廷（Wes Streeting）在周五的一份声明中说：“乌克兰是我们所有人自由的前线。在我最近访问基辅期间，我亲眼目睹了乌克兰人民的勇气与坚韧。”
“我还看到了非凡的创新，正是这些创新让他们得以击退普京非法且无端的入侵。”
斯特里廷说：“这种全球首次获得的真实战场数据访问权限，将使英国公司能够继续推进国防创新的前沿，威慑我们的敌人，让我们在国内更安全，同时也进一步加强乌克兰。”
乌克兰过去曾与盟友分享其源自实战的人工智能训练数据，但这是基辅首次向外国开放其机器学习基础设施的访问权限，而正是这一基础设施推动着前线各地所见的人工智能快速创新。
据乌克兰官员发布的消息，Avengers AI Labs 拥有一个标注数据集，包含超过 500 万个战场帧，以及涵盖数百万次目标检测的传感器数据——包括坦克、火炮、防空系统、步兵、Shahed 无人机、侦察无人机等——主要构建自乌克兰的 DELTA 战场管理系统。
据乌克兰国防部称，数据经过匿名化处理并延迟发布，以避免危及仍在作战的人员。乌克兰国防部还表示，英国公司也在一个安全边界内工作，不允许下载底层数据集。
英国国防部目前正邀请至多12家公司提交方案，说明它们将如何使用该平台，尤其是开发相关技术，使平台即便在通信降级或卫星导航不可用时也能保持完整功能。
英国人工智能大臣卡尼什卡·纳拉扬（Kanishka Narayan）在周五的声明中表示：“这正该工作组旨在推动的那种务实伙伴关系，既支持我们的盟友乌克兰，又增强英国本土的主权能力。”
凯蒂·利文斯通（Katie Livingstone）是《防务新闻》和《军事时报》的乌克兰通讯员。她常驻基辅，自俄罗斯全面入侵最初几天起便持续进行报道。她曾是富布赖特学者，其获奖作品曾在欧洲和美国的多家媒体发表。

items.title: NAVFAC Northwest awards $1 billion multiple award construction contract
items.author: Amanda Surmeier
items.summary: Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Northwest awarded a $1 billion small business indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, multiple-award-construction contract Sept. 24. The majority of the work will take place in Washington state with a Sept. 2028 completion date.
items.body:
Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Northwest awarded a $1 billion small business indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, multiple-award-construction contract Sept. 24. The majority of the work will take place in Washington state with a Sept. 2028 completion date.

This acquisition vehicle arrives on the heels of a record-setting fiscal year in which NAVFAC Northwest already awarded $1 billion in contract actions, reflecting an unprecedented era of recapitalization across regional naval infrastructure.

"This contract positions the Navy and our business partners to move with greater speed and agility throughout the acquisition lifecycle," said Capt. Bob Stiles, NAVFAC Northwest Commanding Officer. "Whether advancing monumental recapitalization efforts under the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP), bolstering the infrastructure that underpins our Navy's Nuclear Deterrence Mission, or executing high-priority military construction and facility sustainment projects, this contracting capability ensures we deliver mission-ready shore platforms to the Fleet when and where they need them the most."

By establishing a pre-qualified pool of vetted small business prime contractors, the MACC substantially shortens procurement lead times for upcoming requirements. Projects awarded under the contract will encompass new design and construction for waterfront facilities, operational infrastructure, industrial support shops, quality of life improvements, and airfield systems, among other scope elements.

For more information on this contract, please contact the NAVFAC Northwest Public Affairs Office at mailto:navfacnwpao@us.navy.mil.

– USN –

Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command is the naval shore facilities, base operating support, and expeditionary engineering systems command that delivers life-cycle technical and acquisition solutions aligned to the fleet and Marine Corps priorities. Follow us at http://www.facebook.com/navfacnorthwest and http://www.linkedin.com/showcase/navfacnorthwest.
zhParas: 美国海军设施工程系统司令部（NAVFAC）西北分部于9月24日授予一份价值10亿美元的小企业不定期交付/不定量、多授标建设合同。大部分工作将在华盛顿州进行，完成日期为2028年9月。
这一采办工具是在一个创纪录财年之后推出的；该财年中，NAVFAC 西北分部已在合同行动中授予10亿美元，反映出整个地区海军基础设施正进入前所未有的资本重组时代。
“这份合同使海军和我们的商业伙伴能够在整个采办生命周期中以更大的速度和灵活性推进，”NAVFAC 西北分部司令鲍勃·斯泰尔斯上校（Capt. Bob Stiles）表示。“无论是在船厂基础设施优化计划（SIOP）下推进重大资本重组工作，加强支撑我们海军核威慑任务的基础设施，还是执行高优先级的军事建设和设施维持项目，这一合同能力都确保我们能在舰队最需要的时间和地点，向其交付可执行任务的岸上平台。”
通过建立一个经过预先资格审查和审核的小企业总承包商池，MACC大幅缩短了未来需求的采购前置时间。根据该合同授予的项目将包括滨水设施、运营基础设施、工业支持车间、生活质量改善和机场系统的新设计与建设，以及其他范围要素。
如需了解该合同的更多信息，请通过 mailto:navfacnwpao@us.navy.mil 联系 NAVFAC 西北分部公共事务办公室。
——美国海军——
美国海军设施工程系统司令部是负责海军岸上设施、基地运营支持和远征工程系统的司令部，提供与舰队和海军陆战队优先事项相一致的全生命周期技术及采办解决方案。请在 http://www.facebook.com/navfacnorthwest 和 http://www.linkedin.com/showcase/navfacnorthwest 关注我们。

items.title: Marine Corps Community Services hosts the 2026 Suicide Prevention Run at Marine Corps Support Facility New Orleans
items.author: Cpl Priscilla Flores
items.summary: U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. Emily Delatorre, a combat graphics specialist with Marine Forces Reserve, smiles at the Run for Them Suicide Prevention Run at Marine Corps Support Facility New Orleans, Sept. 25, 2026. Participants completed a one mile run or walk on the parade deck track in remembrance of those lost to suicide, promoting camaraderie, connection and suicide prevention. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Priscilla Flores)

items.title: From Orbit to Canopy: Guardians explore another frontier in Jungle Operations Training Course- Panama
items.author: SGT Alyssa Norton
items.summary: Maj. Alyson Gleason, assigned to United States Space Force Headquarters, and Capt. Stephen Brown, assigned to 392nd Combat Training Squadron, became the first U.S. Space Force members to complete the Jungle Operations Training Course-Panama, Sept. 25, 2026, at Aeronaval Base Cristóbal Colón.
items.body:
AERONAVAL BASE CRISTÓBAL COLÓN, PANAMA (Sept. 25, 2026) – Maj. Alyson Gleason, assigned to United States Space Force Headquarters, and Capt. Stephen Brown, assigned to 392nd Combat Training Squadron, became the first U.S. Space Force members to complete the Jungle Operations Training Course-Panama, Sept. 25, 2026, at Aeronaval Base Cristóbal Colón.

The 18 day training course placed the Guardians alongside U.S. Army Soldiers and Panamanian partner forces in the jungle of Panama where they were required to learn survival skills such as moving tactically, finding food and operating as a multinational team in the dense jungle environment. Some of the obstacles candidates of JOTC-P have to face are a 5k run, a combat water survival assessment, a knots test and a culminating event testing everything they learn in the course. “I’m always interested in challenging myself and the jungle is a beast that we don’t get to tackle very often as Space Force Officers,” said Gleason. “I saw the opportunity, I wanted the chance to work with the Army and the Panamanian partners down here, and I thought this would be a unique place to challenge myself.” For Guardians, whose main priority is space domain, JOTC-P provides a different environment then they would typically operate in. The Guardians' participation also reflects the expanding opportunities for members of the Space Force to train with other military services and partner nations. Guardians furthering their training outside of their typical job scope creates a stronger organization overall, for Space Force and the U.S. Military as a whole.

“I feel grateful for coming here to the jungle, because I try to go through every experience I can,” said Brown. “Not everybody is going to get the opportunity, so when that door opens I think you should always take it.”

JOTC-P was established as part of a broader U.S.-Panama effort to strengthen security cooperation and interoperability. The course has brought together members of the Army, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force and Panamanian partner forces since its launch. Guardians going through the course is not only a success for Space Force, but for JOTC-P as the course grows in its participation creating stronger, more capable forces across the two nations.

“I think it’s something that if any Space Force person wanted to challenge themselves physically or mentally and get an opportunity to work with the other services this is the place I would do it,” said Gleason. “ It was incredible.”
zhParas: 巴拿马克里斯托瓦尔·科隆海军航空基地（2026年9月25日）——隶属于美国太空军总部的 Maj. 阿莉森·格里森（Alyson Gleason）和隶属于第392战斗训练中队的 Capt. 斯蒂芬·布朗（Stephen Brown），于2026年9月25日在克里斯托瓦尔·科隆海军航空基地成为首批完成巴拿马丛林作战训练课程（JOTC-P）的美国太空军人员。

为期18天的训练课程让这些太空军人员与美陆军士兵和巴拿马伙伴部队一同进入巴拿马丛林，在那里他们必须学习生存技能，例如战术机动、寻找食物，以及在茂密丛林环境中作为多国团队行动。JOTC-P 学员必须面对的一些考验包括5k跑、战斗水上生存评估、绳结测试，以及一场检验课程所学全部内容的结业活动。“我一直乐于挑战自我，而丛林是一头猛兽，作为太空军军官，我们并不常有机会去应对它，”格里森说。“我看到了这个机会，我想获得与陆军以及这里的巴拿马伙伴合作的机会，而且我认为这会是一个挑战自我的独特地方。”对于主要优先事项是太空领域的太空军人员来说，JOTC-P 提供了一个不同于他们通常执行任务的环境。太空军人员的参与也反映出，太空军成员与其他军种和伙伴国家共同训练的机会正在扩大。太空军人员在典型工作范围之外推进训练，从整体上造就了一个更强大的组织，对太空军乃至整个美军都是如此。
“我很感激能来到丛林，因为我努力经历我能经历的每一种体验，”布朗说。“不是每个人都会得到这个机会，所以当那扇门打开时，我认为你应该始终抓住它。”
JOTC-P 是作为美国与巴拿马加强安全合作与互操作性更广泛努力的一部分而设立的。自启动以来，该课程汇聚了陆军、海军陆战队、空军、太空军以及巴拿马伙伴部队的人员。太空军人员参加该课程不仅是太空军的成功，也是 JOTC-P 的成功，因为随着参与规模扩大，该课程正在为两国打造更强大、更有能力的部队。
“我认为，如果任何太空军人员想在身体或精神上挑战自己，并获得与其他军种合作的机会，这里就是我会选择的地方，”格里森说。“这太不可思议了。”

items.title: Laughlin Medical Group hosts first Air Force iCOVER exercise
items.author: SrA Jarrett Smith
items.summary: The Laughlin Medical Group was the first Air Force medical facility to host an exercise focused on iCOVER procedures Sept. 17, 2026.
items.body: In a combat situation, Airmen need to be prepared to help a wingman get back in the fight. However, the effects of combat can extend beyond physical injuries, affecting Airmen mentally and emotionally as well. That’s why iCOVER was introduced: to ensure Airmen are prepared to recognize when a wingman is struggling and help them get the support they need to finish the mission. Now required for deployers and medical personnel, Airmen are trained to provide immediate peer-to-peer support when it matters most. The Laughlin Medical Group was the first Air Force medical facility to host an exercise focused on iCOVER procedures Sept. 17, 2026. During the exercise, Airmen learned the iCOVER framework and applied it hands-on directly in a simulated high-stress scenario. “iCOVER is a critical, peer-to-peer warfighter skillset; essentially "buddy aid" for acute stress, and not a clinical mental health program,” said U.S. Air Force 1st Lt. Caroline Hensley, Laughlin Medical Group executive assistant. “It’s a super easy, six-step technique that anyone can use, completed in 60 seconds.” The technique was developed and trialed by the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research and has been used by militaries in other countries and U.S. Special Forces. In March 2026, the U.S. Air Force and Space Force Surgeon General expanded iCOVER requirements to deployers and medical personnel after the Air Force identified an increase in aeromedical evacuations related to mental health. Following the directive, the Laughlin Medical Group began preparing to introduce the expanded requirement at the local level. “We need more resilient Airmen and we need to give our Airmen the tools to help each other,” said Hensley. “iCOVER gives our Airmen the tools to respond in the complex and ambiguous environments we train for.” During the exercise, Airmen were placed in a simulated combat scenario where they were required to perform both Tactical Combat Casualty Care and iCOVER procedures. Participants were evaluated on their performance and response time. The six-step technique begins with identifying a buddy in need, followed by connecting with their buddy, offering their commitment, verifying facts about the situation, establishing the order of events and finally requesting a specific, mission-related action. “We wanted to ensure members experienced and practiced the scenario as they would in an actual combat scenario,” said Tech. Sgt. Sharome Stafford, Laughlin Operational Medical Readiness SquadronAlcohol and Drug Abuse PreventionNCOIC. “Getting members to see that live in the exercise, they were able to learn and apply it.” After completing the scenario, Airmen practiced relaxation techniques while receiving feedback on their performance. “It was important for us to educate people on the importance of taking care of your own mental health after a stressful situation,” said Hensley. “A lot of times those effects of a stressful situation or an acute stress reaction may show up later.” The Laughlin Medical Group also hosted a Mental Health Symposium running concurrent with the exercise, which was available to participants waiting for their designated training time as well as other members of the Laughlin community. The symposium featured booths where personnel could learn about mental health techniques, available resources and suicide prevention. Helping agencies from across the installation and local community, including the Operational Support Team, Chaplains, Mental Health, Family Advocacy, ADAPT, Sexual Assault & Suicide Prevention, Military and Family Readiness Center, West Texas Counseling, Baptist Child and Family Services, and Military and Family Life Counselingprovided information and demonstrations during the symposium, along with interactive games and prizes. “It’s about making mental health accessible to people, making it more normal and trying to turn it into a warfighter skillset,” said Hensley. “It's kind of like hygiene, or taking care of your brain.” While iCOVER is still in early development, trainers said the event was a success and expressed interest in conducting additional exercises in the future to further familiarize Airmen with the expanded requirement. As the Department of the Air Force rolls out the expanded iCOVER requirements across the force, Laughlin leads the way in ensuring our Airmen are resilient and ready for the fight. “We have a great team and we have the structure for it now,” said Hensley. “As this program continues to be rolled out, there will be more hands-on practice with iCOVER.”
zhParas: 在战斗情况下，空军人员需要准备好帮助战友重新投入战斗。然而，战斗的影响可能超出身体伤害，也会在精神和情感上影响空军人员。因此引入了 iCOVER：确保空军人员准备好识别战友何时陷入困境，并帮助他们获得完成任务所需的支持。如今，该要求适用于部署人员和医务人员，空军人员接受训练，以便在最重要的时刻提供即时同伴互助支持。2026年9月17日，劳克林医疗组成为首个举办以 iCOVER 程序为重点的演习的美国空军医疗机构。演习期间，空军人员学习了 iCOVER 框架，并在模拟的高压场景中直接进行实操应用。“iCOVER 是一项关键的同伴互助作战人员技能；本质上是针对急性应激的‘伙伴救护’，而不是临床心理健康项目，”美国空军 1st Lt. 卡罗琳·亨斯利（Caroline Hensley），劳克林医疗组行政助理说。“这是一种极其简单的六步技术，任何人都可以使用，60 seconds 内即可完成。”该技术由沃尔特·里德陆军研究所开发并试验，并已被其他国家的军队和美国特种部队使用。2026年3月，在空军发现与心理健康相关的航空医疗后送增加后，美国空军和太空军军医长将 iCOVER 要求扩大至部署人员和医务人员。遵照该指令，劳克林医疗组开始准备在本地层面引入扩大后的要求。“我们需要更具韧性的空军人员，也需要为我们的空军人员提供互相帮助的工具，”亨斯利说。“iCOVER 为我们的空军人员提供了在我们所训练的复杂且模糊环境中作出反应的工具。”演习期间，空军人员被置于模拟战斗场景中，要求同时执行战术战伤救治和 iCOVER 程序。参与者根据表现和反应时间接受评估。这六步技术从识别需要帮助的伙伴开始，然后与伙伴建立联系、表达承诺、核实情况事实、确定事件顺序，最后请求采取具体的、与任务相关的行动。“我们想确保成员像在实际战斗场景中那样体验和演练该场景，”劳克林作战医疗战备中队酒精与药物滥用预防士官主管 Tech. Sgt. 沙罗姆·斯塔福德（Sharome Stafford）说。“让成员在演习中现场看到这一点，他们就能够学习并应用它。”完成场景后，空军人员在接受表现反馈的同时练习放松技巧。“对我们来说，重要的是教育人们了解在压力情境后照顾自身心理健康的重要性，”亨斯利说。“很多时候，压力情境的影响或急性应激反应可能会在之后才显现出来。”劳克林医疗组还举办了与演习同期进行的心理健康专题研讨会，面向等待指定训练时间的参与者以及劳克林社区的其他成员开放。研讨会设有展台，人员可以了解心理健康技巧、可用资源和自杀预防。来自整个基地和当地社区的援助机构，包括作战支持团队、随军牧师、心理健康部门、家庭倡导、ADAPT、性侵与自杀预防、军事与家庭准备中心、西得克萨斯咨询、浸信会儿童与家庭服务以及军事与家庭生活咨询，在研讨会期间提供了信息和演示，还设有互动游戏和奖品。“这是为了让人们能够获得心理健康服务，使其更加平常，并努力将其转变为一种作战人员技能，”亨斯利说。“这有点像卫生，或者说照顾你的大脑。”尽管 iCOVER 仍处于早期开发阶段，但训练人员称此次活动取得了成功，并表示有兴趣今后开展更多演习，以进一步让空军人员熟悉扩大后的要求。随着美国空军部在整个部队推行扩大后的 iCOVER 要求，劳克林率先确保我们的空军人员具备韧性并做好战斗准备。“我们有一支优秀的团队，而且我们现在有了相应的组织架构，”亨斯利说。“随着该计划继续推行，将会有更多 iCOVER 实操练习。”

items.body:
National Guard civil support teams, FBI train for chemical, biological threats during Exercise Hellgate at Camp Orchard By Sgt. Rusty Rehl, Idaho Army National Guard Public Affairs

BOISE, Idaho – National Guard civil support teams from four states joined the FBI, Army National Guard aviation crews and law enforcement officers for a mock raid on simulated chemical and biological laboratories Sept. 22-23 at the Idaho Army National Guard’s Camp Orchard.

Participating teams included the Utah National Guard’s 85th CST, the South Dakota National Guard’s 82nd CST, the Arizona National Guard’s 91st CST and the Idaho National Guard’s 101st CST. Decontamination teams from all four CSTs set up joint lines to process tactical teams and simulated casualties coming out of contaminated areas, while medical sections tracked symptoms and coordinated evacuation.

Local and regional law enforcement partners included the Boise Police Department, Boise Fire Department, Ada County Sheriff’s Office, Idaho State Police and Salt Lake City police officers.

“Having the county sheriff’s office, also with your local PD, and then having your FBI all here together and understanding each other’s capabilities has been awesome,” Lt. Col. Ryan Morrissey said, commander of the Arizona National Guard’s 91st CST.

The raid was a centerpiece of Exercise Hellgate, a four-day, multiagency exercise Sept. 21-24 designed to test how National Guard Weapons of Mass Destruction-Civil Support Teams, federal agents and first responders work together against a chemical, biological or radiological attack on a community.

CH-47 Chinook crews from the Nevada Army National Guard’s B Company, 1st Battalion, 189th Aviation Regiment, along with Idaho Army National Guard crews from the 1st Battalion, 183rd Aviation Regiment, flew teams and simulated casualties between Gowen Field and landing zones at Camp Orchard.

“Having the capabilities to get on a military helicopter with some of the federal partners like FBI, that’s just been awesome,” said Morrissey, “The training value has been great to exercise that strike package.”

For many participants, the exercise marked the first time their units had worked side by side. A major focus was getting each agency’s communications systems connected so teams could share a common picture of the threat in real time.

“That’s always a challenge, because everyone has different common operating pictures, different software they use, different systems that they use,” Morrissey said. “So it’s been good, because this has really tested us in feeding in the information together and understanding each other’s ways they’re communicating from a tactical standpoint to then also at our tactical operations centers.”

Exercise planners built the scenario around a fictional extremist network plotting coordinated attacks on public venues across the Treasure Valley. Throughout the week, joint teams of CST members, FBI bomb technicians, K-9 handlers and police officers practiced hazard assessments at simulated event sites before the exercise moved to Camp Orchard.

At Camp Orchard’s Combined Arms Collective Training Facility, FBI SWAT teams cleared buildings staged as clandestine laboratories. CST survey teams followed, screening for hazards, collecting and packaging samples and maintaining chain of custody for evidence.

Beyond building relationships, the exercise allowed the CST teams to test newly developed decontamination and joint hazard assessment procedures. Lessons learned will be used to refine those procedures ahead of future large-scale security missions.

“My favorite part of it from my level as a commander is just being able to be engaged and be part of the planning process and the response planning process at all the different levels,” Morrissey said. “Either it be you know state assets or it be the federal partners, and just understanding their planning and procedures on how they're tackling some of these complex situations.”

Weapons of Mass Destruction-Civil Support Teams are full-time National Guard units made up of Army and Air National Guard members. The teams support civil authorities by identifying chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive hazards, assessing their effects, advising incident commanders and helping coordinate additional state and federal support.

国民警卫队民事支援小组与FBI在奥查德营举行的“地狱门”演习中开展化学、生物威胁应对训练
作者：爱达荷陆军国民警卫队公共事务部 Sgt. Rusty Rehl
爱达荷州博伊西——来自四个州的国民警卫队民事支援小组与FBI、陆军国民警卫队航空机组及执法人员一道，于9月22日至23日在爱达荷陆军国民警卫队奥查德营（Camp Orchard）对模拟化学与生物实验室实施了突袭演练。
参演小组包括犹他国民警卫队第85民事支援小组（85th CST）、南达科他国民警卫队第82民事支援小组（82nd CST）、亚利桑那国民警卫队第91民事支援小组（91st CST）和爱达荷国民警卫队第101民事支援小组（101st CST）。四个民事支援小组的洗消分队设立联合洗消线，负责处理从污染区撤出的战术小组和模拟伤员，医疗部门则追踪症状并协调后送。
地方及区域执法伙伴包括博伊西警察局、博伊西消防局、阿达县治安官办公室、爱达荷州警察局以及盐湖城警员。
“把县治安官办公室、当地警察局以及FBI都聚到一起，了解彼此的能力，这非常棒，”亚利桑那国民警卫队第91民事支援小组指挥官 Lt. Col. Ryan Morrissey 说。
此次突袭是“地狱门”演习的核心课目。该演习于9月21日至24日举行，为期四天、多机构参与，旨在检验国民警卫队大规模杀伤性武器民事支援小组、联邦探员与一线应急人员如何协同应对针对社区实施的化学、生物或放射性袭击。
来自内华达陆军国民警卫队第189航空团第1营B连的CH-47 Chinook直升机机组，以及爱达荷陆军国民警卫队第183航空团第1营的机组，在高文机场（Gowen Field）与奥查德营的着陆场之间运送参演小组和模拟伤员。
“能够登上军用直升机，与FBI等联邦伙伴一同行动，这真的非常棒，”Morrissey说，“这次训练在演练该打击编组方面的价值非常大。”
对许多参演人员来说，这次演习标志着他们所在部队首次并肩协作。一个主要重点是把各机构的通信系统连接起来，以便各团队能够实时共享共同的威胁态势图。
“这始终是个挑战，因为每个人都有不同的共同作战态势图，使用不同的软件，使用不同的系统，”莫里西（Morrissey）说。“所以这很好，因为这真正考验了我们共同输入信息，并从战术角度以及在我们的战术作战中心理解彼此的通信方式。”
演习策划者围绕一个虚构的极端主义网络构建了想定，该网络策划对特雷热谷各地公共场馆发动协同袭击。整整一周，由CST成员、联邦调查局（FBI）排爆技术人员、K-9训导员和警察组成的联合小组在模拟活动场所进行危害评估，随后演习转移到奥查德营。
在奥查德营的合成兵种集体训练设施，FBI特警队清剿了被布置成秘密实验室的建筑物。CST勘察队随后跟进，筛查危险物、收集并包装样本，并维护证据保管链。
除了建立关系之外，这次演习还让CST团队得以测试新开发的洗消与联合危害评估程序。所吸取的经验教训将用于在未来的大规模安全任务之前完善这些程序。
“从我这个指挥官的层级来看，我最喜欢的部分就是能够参与其中，并成为各个不同层级规划过程和响应规划过程的一部分，”莫里西说。“无论是州级资源，还是联邦合作伙伴，就是能够了解他们在应对其中一些复杂情况时的规划和程序。”
大规模杀伤性武器民事支援分队（Weapons of Mass Destruction-Civil Support Teams）是全日制国民警卫队部队，由陆军国民警卫队和空军国民警卫队成员组成。这些分队通过识别化学、生物、放射、核与爆炸物危害，评估其影响，向事件指挥官提供建议，并帮助协调额外的州和联邦支援，来支持民事当局。

“把县治安官办公室、当地警察局以及FBI都聚到一起，了解彼此的能力，这非常棒，”亚利桑那国民警卫队第91民事支援小组指挥官 Lt. Col. Ryan Morrissey 说。

此次突袭是“地狱门”演习的核心课目。该演习于9月21日至24日举行，为期四天、多机构参与，旨在检验国民警卫队大规模杀伤性武器民事支援小组、联邦探员与一线应急人员如何协同应对针对社区实施的化学、生物或放射性袭击。

来自内华达陆军国民警卫队第189航空团第1营B连的CH-47 Chinook直升机机组，以及爱达荷陆军国民警卫队第183航空团第1营的机组，在高文机场（Gowen Field）与奥查德营的着陆场之间运送参演小组和模拟伤员。

“能够登上军用直升机，与FBI等联邦伙伴一同行动，这真的非常棒，”Morrissey说，“这次训练在演练该打击编组方面的价值非常大。”

对许多参演人员来说，这次演习标志着他们所在部队首次并肩协作。一个主要重点是把各机构的通信系统连接起来，以便各团队能够实时共享共同的威胁态势图。

“这始终是个挑战，因为每个人都有不同的共同作战态势图，使用不同的软件，使用不同的系统，”莫里西（Morrissey）说。“所以这很好，因为这真正考验了我们共同输入信息，并从战术角度以及在我们的战术作战中心理解彼此的通信方式。”

演习策划者围绕一个虚构的极端主义网络构建了想定，该网络策划对特雷热谷各地公共场馆发动协同袭击。整整一周，由CST成员、联邦调查局（FBI）排爆技术人员、K-9训导员和警察组成的联合小组在模拟活动场所进行危害评估，随后演习转移到奥查德营。

在奥查德营的合成兵种集体训练设施，FBI特警队清剿了被布置成秘密实验室的建筑物。CST勘察队随后跟进，筛查危险物、收集并包装样本，并维护证据保管链。

除了建立关系之外，这次演习还让CST团队得以测试新开发的洗消与联合危害评估程序。所吸取的经验教训将用于在未来的大规模安全任务之前完善这些程序。

“从我这个指挥官的层级来看，我最喜欢的部分就是能够参与其中，并成为各个不同层级规划过程和响应规划过程的一部分，”莫里西说。“无论是州级资源，还是联邦合作伙伴，就是能够了解他们在应对其中一些复杂情况时的规划和程序。”

大规模杀伤性武器民事支援分队（Weapons of Mass Destruction-Civil Support Teams）是全日制国民警卫队部队，由陆军国民警卫队和空军国民警卫队成员组成。这些分队通过识别化学、生物、放射、核与爆炸物危害，评估其影响，向事件指挥官提供建议，并帮助协调额外的州和联邦支援，来支持民事当局。

items.title: USSPACECOM hosts third wargame series focused on maneuver warfare in the space domain
items.author: PO1 Shannon Burns
items.summary: U.S. Space Command held its third APOLLO INSIGHT Commercial Integration Wargame exercise on September 23, 2026.
items.body: U.S. Space Command held its third APOLLO INSIGHT Commercial Integration Wargame exercise on September 23, 2026. The third of four Commercial Integration tabletop exercises (TTX) focused on diversified orbits and included multiple scenarios and goals. Participants collaborated on shared strategies, improved their communication, and generated innovative ideas for future commercial capabilities. “Our first two Commercial Integration Wargame TTXs generated high interest from across the DoW [Department of War] and industry partners. We’ve received positive responses for this third TTX, and we welcome the collaboration with commercial partners to find resilient and diversified solutions that address command priorities,” Cmdr. Heather Thomas, Commercial Integration Branch Chief for USSPACECOM’s Capability and Resource Integration directorate said prior to the event. “For this upcoming exercise we currently have 217 participants registered representing 87 different companies, including 24 new additions since our first and second events. Thanks to the great participation and collaboration during the first two exercises, we’ve been able to set a very high bar, and I expect that as we continue the commercial integration in exercises into 2027, interest will continue to increase." Retired Brig. Gen. Bruce McClintock, RAND senior policy researcher and Space Enterprise Initiative lead, who was the moderator for this third TTX, said he was impressed by USSPACECOM’s commitment to information sharing and integration capabilities into campaigning and operations. “The United States is stronger when it works closely with allies, partners and commercial providers,” said McClintock. “SPACECOM’s commitment to increased integration through these TTX events reflects a tangible effort to grow those important relationships and strengthen a broader coalition of allies, partners, and commercial providers.” He added, “TTX #3 was noteworthy for the detailed discussion and information sharing among participants developing non-Keplerian space capabilities, further diversifying the orbits used for a wide range of activities. I was encouraged that a variety of commercial partners are making important advances in vLEO [Very Low Earth Orbit] and cislunar capabilities. The problem sets examined during APOLLO INSIGHT could be tested through combined maneuvers to further develop TTPs [Tactics, Techniques and Procedures] across the space enterprise.” During an appearance Fed Gov Today on August 30, 2026, Gen. Stephen Whiting, USSPACECOM commander, emphasized the need to integrate with not only the United States’ allies and partners, but with commercial industry companies as well. “Space is just so vast that we can’t do it all alone inside our own command. No single country, no single service, no single agency, no single company can do all the things we have to do in space to be successful. When we think of integration, we’re thinking about how to partner with different stakeholders,” Whiting said. “The U.S. commercial space industry is a massive advantage for our nation, and we’ve got to be able to leverage their cost curves and their innovation points.” He added that there is an urgent need to integrate allied and commercial capabilities, deepen partnerships with industry for space domain awareness, and harness AI and machine learning to outpace adversaries in closing surveillance gaps. Thomas added that they are planning the fourth and final TTX of the year, scheduled for December 16th at the Aerospace Corporation, adding that they have been a great host for each of these APOLLO INSIGHT events this year. The first and second TTXs in the series were held in Colorado Springs, Colorado on March 23 and June 24, 2026, and centered on the threat of weapons of mass destruction in space and maneuver warfare respectively. To read about the first TTX in the series go to: [https://www.spacecom.mil/Newsroom/News/Article-Display/Article/4451258/usspacecom-executes-inaugural-apollo-insight-commercial-integration-wargame-ser/](https://www.spacecom.mil/Newsroom/News/Article-Display/Article/4451258/usspacecom-executes-inaugural-apollo-insight-commercial-integration-wargame-ser/) To read about the second TTX in the series go to: [https://www.spacecom.mil/Newsroom/News/Article-Display/Article/4528685/usspacecom-hosts-second-wargame-series-focused-on-maneuver-warfare-in-the-space/](https://www.spacecom.mil/Newsroom/News/Article-Display/Article/4528685/usspacecom-hosts-second-wargame-series-focused-on-maneuver-warfare-in-the-space/) For information about USSPACECOM’s industry engagement or to explore opportunities to participate in future campaigning with commercial programs, please visit: [https://www.spacecom.mil/Partnerships-and-Outreach/Industry-Engagement-Portal/](https://www.spacecom.mil/Partnerships-and-Outreach/Industry-Engagement-Portal/)
zhParas: 美国太空司令部于2026年9月23日举行了第三次APOLLO INSIGHT商业整合兵棋演习。这是四次商业整合桌面演习（TTX）中的第三次，聚焦多样化轨道，并包含多个想定和目标。参与者就共同战略开展协作，改进沟通，并为未来商业能力提出创新想法。“我们前两次商业整合兵棋TTX在战争部（DoW）和行业伙伴中引发了高度关注。我们对这第三次TTX也收到了积极反馈，并欢迎与商业伙伴合作，寻找有韧性且多样化的解决方案，以应对司令部优先事项，”美国太空司令部（USSPACECOM）能力与资源整合局商业整合处处长 Cmdr. Heather Thomas（希瑟·托马斯）在活动前表示。“对于即将举行的这次演习，我们目前已有217名注册参与者，代表87家不同公司，其中包括自我们第一次和第二次活动以来新增的24家。得益于前两次演习中的出色参与和协作，我们得以设定很高的标准，我预计随着我们在2027年继续将商业整合纳入演习，兴趣将继续增加。”第三次TTX的主持人、兰德公司高级政策研究员兼太空企业倡议负责人、退役 Brig. Gen. Bruce McClintock（布鲁斯·麦克林托克）表示，美国太空司令部对信息共享以及将能力整合到战役和行动中的承诺给他留下了深刻印象。“美国与盟友、伙伴和商业供应商密切合作时会更强大，”麦克林托克说。“太空司令部通过这些TTX活动加强整合的承诺，体现了为发展这些重要关系并强化由盟友、伙伴和商业供应商组成的更广泛联盟所作出的切实努力。”他补充说：“第三次TTX值得注意，参与者围绕发展非开普勒太空能力进行了详细讨论和信息共享，进一步使广泛活动所使用的轨道多样化。令我感到鼓舞的是，各类商业伙伴正在vLEO（极低地球轨道）和地月空间能力方面取得重要进展。APOLLO INSIGHT期间审视的问题集可以通过联合机动进行测试，以在整个太空事业中进一步发展TTP（战术、技术和程序）。”在2026年8月30日做客《Fed Gov Today》节目时，美国太空司令部司令 Gen. Stephen Whiting（斯蒂芬·惠廷）强调，不仅需要与美国盟友和伙伴整合，也需要与商业航天企业整合。“太空如此辽阔，我们无法仅靠自己的司令部完成所有事情。没有任何单一国家、单一军种、单一机构、单一公司能够完成我们在太空要取得成功必须做的所有事情。当我们考虑整合时，我们考虑的是如何与不同利益相关方合作，”惠廷说。“美国商业航天产业是我们国家的巨大优势，我们必须能够利用他们的成本曲线和创新点。”他补充说，迫切需要整合盟友和商业能力，深化与业界在太空域感知方面的伙伴关系，并利用人工智能和机器学习，在弥合监视缺口方面超越对手。托马斯补充说，他们正筹划今年的第四次、也是最后一次TTX，定于12月16日在 Aerospace Corporation 举行，并补充说该公司今年一直是这些APOLLO INSIGHT活动的出色东道主。该系列第一次和第二次TTX分别于2026年3月23日和6月24日在科罗拉多州科罗拉多斯普林斯举行，重点分别是太空中的大规模杀伤性武器威胁和机动战。如需了解该系列第一次TTX，请访问：https://www.spacecom.mil/Newsroom/News/Article-Display/Article/4451258/usspacecom-executes-inaugural-apollo-insight-commercial-integration-wargame-ser/ 如需了解该系列第二次TTX，请访问：https://www.spacecom.mil/Newsroom/News/Article-Display/Article/4528685/usspacecom-hosts-second-wargame-series-focused-on-maneuver-warfare-in-the-space/ 如需了解美国太空司令部的行业接触情况，或探索参与未来与商业项目共同开展行动的机会，请访问：https://www.spacecom.mil/Partnerships-and-Outreach/Industry-Engagement-Portal/

items.title: Maj. Spingarn Heads to Naples (30 SEP 1943)
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: On Sept. 30, 1943, Maj. Stephen J. Spingarn and his 305th Counter Intelligence Corps (CIC) Detachment prepared to enter Naples along the Italian coast. Throughout September, Spingarn and his agents had moved from a reactive unit supporting frontline troops to a strong counterintelligence presence for the Fifth Army.
items.body:
On Sept. 30, 1943, Maj. Stephen J. Spingarn and his 305th Counter Intelligence Corps (CIC) Detachment prepared to enter Naples along the Italian coast. Throughout September, Spingarn and his agents had moved from a reactive unit supporting frontline troops to a strong counterintelligence presence for the Fifth Army.

In the weeks leading up to their entry into the city, Spingarn had expanded CIC activities far beyond the beachhead where the detachment first found itself under heavy enemy fire. Spingarn, then 35 years old, had gained experience at Allied Force Headquarters planning Mediterranean operations, which shaped how the Fifth Army’s CIC adapted to the fluid conditions of the Italian campaign. After assuming command of the Fifth Army CIC Detachment—later formally designated the 305th CIC Section—in August 1943, he organized his men for deployment from Oran, Algeria, on Sept. 1. To protect the unit during the 850-mile journey, personnel were carefully dispersed among several vessels.

Their arrival at the Salerno beachhead on Sept. 11 placed the detachment immediately in the line of fire. Spingarn and his agents established makeshift operations from foxholes, often finding themselves ahead of the American infantry. In one instance, as Spingarn later recalled, two German tanks advanced to within 100 yards of their position and opened fire with machine guns and 88-mm cannon. Only a slight rise in the ground—“perhaps a foot high,” he noted—kept the machine-gun rounds inches above their heads as they flattened themselves against the earth.

As the Fifth Army pushed outward from the beachhead, the CIC detachment gradually shifted from mere survival toward active counterintelligence work. With greater freedom of movement, agents began interrogating wounded and captured Italian and German soldiers, along with numerous Italian civilians. These early investigations revealed valuable information: Agent Merle V. Ploghoft identified German plans for a major defensive stand at Bologna, tracked enemy troop movements from Benevento, and uncovered Italian collaborators assisting the Axis.

By mid-to-late September, Spingarn broadened CIC reach beyond the mainland. He conducted a survey of offshore islands and assigned Agent Donald M. Funk to establish CIC presence on Capri. At the same time, Spingarn met with prominent anti-Fascist figures, including Senator Benedetto Croce and Col. Tito Zaniboni, the World War I hero who had attempted to assassinate Mussolini in 1925, to cultivate cooperation and lay foundations for resistance networks. These connections and assessments strengthened the Fifth Army’s CI posture as Allied forces advanced northward.

Toward the end of the month, the Fifth Army G-2, Col. Edwin H. Howard, directed Spingarn to be prepared to enter Naples immediately upon its fall. Spingarn coordinated with the 82d Airborne Division and the British Field Security Police to assemble a convoy of eight jeeps, four trucks, and fourteen motorcycles, carrying sixteen CIC agents and nineteen Field Security Policemen.

With Naples finally opening to Allied occupation on Oct. 1, Spingarn’s detachment poised itself for a new phase of operations. The previous nineteen days had been marked by constant forward movement—entering towns, interviewing officials, establishing temporary systems, and then pushing on with advancing troops. Naples offered the first opportunity for sustained static counterintelligence coverage. There, CIC agents could build and maintain informant networks, investigate leads in depth, and provide comprehensive security oversight. As later reports noted, these efforts produced “in most cases, definite results.”

For more on Major Spingarn's work in Italy, see: https://www.dvidshub.net/news/458064/tactical-ci-italy-nov-1944

Article by Michael E. Bigelow, INSCOM Command Historian. New issues of This Week in MI History are published each week. To report story errors, ask questions, request previous articles, or be added to our distribution list, please contact: TR-ICoE-Command-Historian@army.mil.
zhParas: 1943年9月30日，Maj. 斯蒂芬·J·斯平加恩（Stephen J. Spingarn）及其第305反情报部队（CIC）分遣队准备沿意大利海岸进入那不勒斯。整个9月，斯平加恩及其特工人员已从一支支援前线部队的被动反应部队，转变为第五集团军的一支强大的反情报力量。

在进入该市之前的数周里，斯平加恩已将CIC活动远远扩展到该分遣队最初在敌军猛烈火力下所处滩头阵地之外。斯平加恩时年35岁，曾在盟军司令部规划地中海行动，这段经历影响了第五集团军CIC如何适应意大利战役中多变的形势。1943年8月，他在接掌第五集团军CIC分遣队——后正式定名为第305 CIC分队——后，于9月1日组织手下从阿尔及利亚奥兰出发部署。为在850-mile的行程中保护该部队，人员被小心分散到多艘船只上。
他们于9月11日抵达萨莱诺滩头阵地，使该分遣队立即置身火线。斯平加恩及其特工人员从散兵坑中建立临时行动点，常常发现自己位于美国步兵前方。斯平加恩后来回忆，有一次两辆德军坦克推进到距他们阵地100 yards以内，并用机枪和88-mm火炮开火。只有地面上一处微微隆起——“perhaps a foot high，”他指出——在他们俯卧于地时，使机枪子弹从他们头顶上方几inches处掠过。
随着第五集团军从滩头阵地向外推进，CIC分遣队逐渐从仅仅求生存转向积极的反情报工作。随着行动自由度增大，特工人员开始审讯负伤和被俘的意大利及德国士兵，以及大量意大利平民。这些早期调查揭示了有价值的信息：特工梅尔·V·普洛格霍夫特（Merle V. Ploghoft）查明德军计划在博洛尼亚进行重大防御战，追踪了敌军从贝内文托开始的调动，并揭露了协助轴心国的意大利通敌者。

到9月中下旬，斯平加恩将CIC的触及范围扩大到大陆以外。他对近海岛屿进行了勘察，并指派特工唐纳德·M·芬克（Donald M. Funk）在卡普里岛建立CIC存在。与此同时，斯平加恩会见了知名反法西斯人物，包括参议员贝内代托·克罗齐（Benedetto Croce）和Col.蒂托·扎尼博尼（Tito Zaniboni）——这位第一次世界大战英雄曾于1925年试图刺杀墨索里尼（Mussolini）——以培养合作并为抵抗网络奠定基础。随着盟军向北推进，这些联系和评估加强了第五集团军的CI态势。
临近月底，第五集团军G-2、Col.埃德温·H·霍华德（Edwin H. Howard）指示斯平加恩做好准备，一旦那不勒斯陷落就立即进入该市。斯平加恩与第82空降师和英国战地安全警察协调，组建了一支由8辆吉普车、4辆卡车和14辆摩托车组成的车队，运载16名CIC特工和19名战地安全警察。
随着那不勒斯最终于10月1日被盟军占领，斯平加恩的分遣队为进入新一阶段行动做好准备。此前的19天以持续向前推进为特点——进入城镇、访谈官员、建立临时体系，然后随推进部队继续前进。那不勒斯首次提供了持续静态反情报覆盖的机会。在那里，CIC特工可以建立并维持线人网络，深入调查线索，并提供全面的安全监督。正如后来报告所指出的，这些努力“在多数情况下取得了明确结果”。

items.title: Trump administration obligates $307M for military aid to Ukraine
items.author: Patricia Zengerle and Mike Stone, Reuters
items.summary: The Trump administration has made legally binding commitments to spend almost all of the $400 million Congress approved for military aid to Ukraine.
items.body:
The Trump administration has made legally binding commitments to spend almost all of the $400 million Congress approved for military aid to Ukraine late last year, ensuring that the money will not expire on Sept. 30, according to three sources familiar with the plan.

As of early this week, $307 million of the $400 million of the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative (USAI) funding had been obligated, said the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, and the administration plans to lock in the remaining $93 million before the fiscal year ends on Sept. 30.

The Pentagon, which oversees the USAI program, declined to comment for this story.

First deliveries include weapons, spare parts

The money has been a source of contention with Congress, as Democrats and some of President Donald Trump’s fellow Republicans have criticized the Pentagon for sitting on the aid for Kyiv, which members of both parties voted for last December.

Trump has in recent months taken a more positive tone toward Ukraine, signing off on a proposal to give a license for Ukraine to manufacture Patriot interceptor missiles and signing a Russia sanctions bill.

He met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy this week at UN headquarters in New York, after which Zelenskiy said they had discussed efforts to end the war with Russia, including a potential bilateral ceasefire on energy-related targets.

The first deliveries, which will include offensive weapons and equipment such as spare parts for armored vehicles, began this month. The rest are expected to be delivered before October 2029, the sources said. Trump’s White House term ends in January of that year.

The remaining $93 million in the package approved by Congress does not have to be spent by the end of the year, but it will expire if it is not formally placed under contract by then.

Patriot missiles not included

One of the sources said the military equipment did not include Patriot missiles, despite Russia bombarding Ukraine’s cities with drones and ballistic missiles.

The U.S. war in Iran and the Ukraine war have depleted global supplies of Patriots, and Kyiv has been pleading for more.

Reuters reported in July that the administration had told Congress it could take years for the equipment to reach Ukrainian forces. The Pentagon has held up shipments of weapons to Ukraine several times out of concern that US weapons supplies were too low.

Lawmakers said then they were unhappy with the Pentagon’s timeline, considered unusually slow for an ongoing conflict, and the issue has come up repeatedly at congressional hearings.

Ukraine has been by far the top recipient of U.S. foreign aid since Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, but the U.S. commitment to Kyiv has been called into question since Trump took office and his Republicans took control of both houses of Congress in January 2025.
zhParas: 据三位了解该计划的消息人士称，特朗普政府已做出具有法律约束力的承诺，将把国会去年年底批准的4亿美元对乌军事援助资金几乎全部支出，确保这笔钱不会在9月30日到期作废。
消息人士称，截至本周初，乌克兰安全援助倡议（USAI）4亿美元资金中已有3.07亿美元完成拨付；这些要求匿名的消息人士表示，政府计划在9月30日本财年结束前锁定剩余的9300万美元。
负责监管USAI项目的五角大楼拒绝对此事置评。
首批交付包括武器和备件
这笔资金一直是与国会争执的焦点：民主党人和特朗普总统的一些共和党同僚批评五角大楼迟迟不发放对基辅的援助，而两党议员去年12月都投票支持了这笔援助。
近几个月，特朗普对乌克兰的语气更为积极，批准了一项允许乌克兰生产 Patriot 拦截导弹的提案，并签署了一项对俄制裁法案。
本周他在纽约联合国总部会见了乌克兰总统泽连斯基（Volodymyr Zelenskiy），会后泽连斯基表示，双方讨论了结束与俄罗斯战争的努力，包括可能就能源相关目标达成双边停火。
首批交付于本月开始，其中包括进攻性武器以及装甲车辆备件等装备。消息人士称，其余部分预计将在2029年10月前交付完毕。特朗普的白宫任期将于当年1月结束。
国会批准的这项一揽子计划中剩余的 9300 万美元无需在年底前支出，但如果届时未正式签订合同，这笔资金将失效。
未包含“爱国者”导弹
其中一名消息人士称，这批军事装备不包括“爱国者”导弹，尽管俄罗斯正用无人机和弹道导弹轰炸乌克兰的城市。
美国在伊朗的战争以及乌克兰战争已使全球“爱国者”导弹的库存消耗殆尽，基辅一直在恳求获得更多。
路透社 7 月报道称，该届政府已告知国会，这批装备可能需要数年时间才能送达乌克兰军队。由于担心美国武器库存过低，五角大楼已多次推迟向乌克兰运送武器。
议员们当时表示，他们对五角大楼的时间表感到不满，认为对于一场正在进行的冲突而言这一进度异常缓慢，该问题已在国会听证会上被反复提及。
自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯发动全面入侵以来，乌克兰一直是美国对外援助的最大受援国，且远超其他国家和地区；但自特朗普（Trump）就职、其所属共和党于 2025 年 1 月控制国会两院以来，美国对基辅的承诺便受到质疑。

items.title: Royal Australian Navy Divers Train at Pearl Harbor for U.S. Virginia-class Submarine Sustainment
items.author: Ashley Calingo
items.summary: Inside the flooded ballast tanks of a Virginia-class submarine, where there is no natural light and spaces are tighter than shoulder-width, Royal Australian Navy divers are learning how to sustain one of the world’s most advanced undersea platforms. Though the work is gritty, technical and claustrophobic, it represents one of the clearest signs yet that AUKUS—the enhanced security partnership between Australia, the U.S. and the U.K.—is progressing and delivering results.
items.body:
JOINT BASE PEARL HARBOR-HICKAM, Hawaii— Inside the flooded ballast tanks of a Virginia-class submarine, where there is no natural light and spaces are tighter than shoulder-width, Royal Australian Navy divers are learning how to sustain one of the world’s most advanced undersea platforms. Though the work is gritty, technical and claustrophobic, it represents one of the clearest signs yet that AUKUS—the enhanced security partnership between Australia, the U.S. and the U.K.—is progressing and delivering results.

“It’s really exciting to be part of the first group of divers to receive this training in the U.S. for a new capability back in Australia,” said Royal Australian Navy Lieutenant Cantona*. “Usually in the military you’ve got your [standard operating procedures] and structures, but here we’re essentially creating something brand new, which is very unique and rare.”

Cantona is one of eight Australian divers who underwent an immersive five-month training rotation at Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PHNSY & IMF). They were the first Australian divers trained to maintain U.S. nuclear-powered attack submarines at the same level as American Sailors and shipyard personnel. Their mission involved learning the skills needed to execute diver operations on Virginia-class submarines in Australia.

“It’s a privilege to be here,” said Cantona during his training in Hawaii. “We’re laying the groundwork for a future force—one that can keep submarines ready, at sea and on mission from the Indian Ocean.”

The training is both physically demanding and technically rigorous. Each diver was fully integrated with U.S. Navy dive teams, executing underwater work that includes component swaps inside ballast tanks, torpedo tube inspections, fly-by-wire system checks and rigging operations. They also completed radiological diver certification and shipyard safety qualifications.

“We treated them like one of our own,” said Chief Warrant Officer Michael Tuft, command diving officer at PHNSY & IMF. “No special treatment. They’re on our teams, doing the same dives, attending the same briefs, the same post-job cleanup. And they crushed it.”

Tuft said the Royal Australian Navy divers were paired in two-person teams and assigned directly to U.S. dive lockers, giving them immediate exposure to the rhythm of day-to-day maintenance operations. While the clearance diving branch, the specialized diving unit of the Royal Australian Navy, is no stranger to complex undersea tasks, nuclear submarine maintenance introduces new technical demands.

“You can’t just drydock a sub every time something breaks,” said Tuft. “A lot of the work—especially inside the ballast tanks—has to happen in the water. And not just anyone can do that. You need divers trained to this level of precision, with this level of trust.”

Trust is a recurrent theme in the diving community and throughout the broader AUKUS partnership. Below the surface, there is no room for second-guessing. “The person beside you is your backup. You’ve got to know they’ll be there if something goes wrong,” said Royal Australian Navy Able Seaman Finn. “What’s amazing is that the U.S. teams gave us that trust from the start—and we’ve earned it.”

That trust is essential not just for safety, but for strategic readiness. As the U.S., U.K. and Australia continue implementing AUKUS Pillar I, interoperability is no longer a future goal—it is a present requirement.

Over the past year, the Australian divers were able to demonstrate their skill during two major AUKUS submarine maintenance periods. First, during the U.S.’s maintenance period for USS Vermont’s (SSN 792) in November 2025, then again during the U.K.’s maintenance period for HMS Anson in February 2026. Both maintenance availabilities, which took place at HMAS Stirling in Western Australia, support Australia’s long-term goal of building a sovereign sustainment capability for nuclear-powered submarines, a key requirement for AUKUS. The Australian divers will have another opportunity to demonstrate their skills at the U.S. Navy’s next planned submarine maintenance period before the end of this year.

At the AUKUS Defense Ministers' Meeting in May 2026, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Australia’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence Richard Marles, and the U.K.’s Secretary of State for Defence John Healey confirmed that AUKUS Pillar I remained on track. In their joint statement, the defense ministers also announced that key milestones were being met to establish Submarine Rotational Forces-West (SRF-West) as early as 2027. Under SRF-West, U.S. and U.K. nuclear-powered attack submarines will conduct rotational deployments from HMAS Stirling. As part of SRF-West, Australian maintenance workers—including these newly trained Royal Australian Navy divers—will play an increasing role in maintenance activities as they continue building the expertise to operate and sustain their own fleet of attack submarines.

“This is one of the most important building blocks of SRF-West,” said Elizabeth Tolin, deputy division head for SRF-West at the AUKUS Integration & Acquisition program office. “Ultimately, most of the sustainment work will be done by Australians. We’re training them to our standards now, so we can operate together with confidence anywhere in the world.”

Tolin, who helped establish the diver training pipeline, said this effort required transforming PHNSY & IMF into an international training venue, a first for naval shipyards. PHNSY &IMF, which was previously named the lead maintenance activity for SRF-West, will establish a maintenance detachment in Western Australia where American maintainers there will continue working alongside their Australian counterparts.

“We had to build the machinery—curriculum, systems, policy—before we could even put students in the water,” Tolin said. “What you’re seeing now is a partner stepping up with speed and precision.”

The partnership is built not just on shared values, but on operational necessity.

“Well, if submarines break, they can’t always come back to Hawaii,” Tuft said. “If they’re near Australia, they can pull in there, and we know that we’ve trained the Australians to the same U.S. standards. They can fix that submarine and get it back on the front lines.”

“SRF-West is the cornerstone for AUKUS Pillar I,” said Rear Adm. Doug Adams, director, AUKUS, International and Systems. “For the U.S. Navy, conducting rotational deployments out of HMAS Stirling reduces transit times, increases attack-submarine presence and delivers peace through strength in the Indo-Pacific region. Building the maintenance capability in Australia will keep our submarines fit to fight and prepares the Royal Australian Navy and its sustainment partners to work on their own future fleet of conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines.”

According to Tuft, this training is creating a flexible and resilient workforce across the Indo-Pacific.

“If we’re overwhelmed, we can call [the Australians] and say, ‘Hey, can you send me six people?’ They can do the same with us. That’s the kind of partnership we’re building. We can support each other with everything.”

For the Australian divers, the experience is as personal as it is professional.

“Diving inside a submarine’s ballast tanks, shoulder to the wall, with no visibility—it gets the heart rate going,” said Finn. “But it’s a massive privilege to gain these skills and help stand up something this important from day one.”

Tuft said few people outside of the program understand the scale of what is being built.

“This is one of the first times we’ve ever trained foreign partners to maintain our submarines,” he said. “It says everything about the strength of our alliance and how much we trust Australians to help carry it forward.”

As the divers prepared to return to Australia and support future submarine maintenance periods, Cantona said the most important work may still be ahead.

“We’ll need to rewrite some policies, update training manuals, build the infrastructure to scale what we’ve learned here,” he said. “But we’re ready for that. We’ve got the backing. We’ve got the knowledge. Now we’re going to make it ours.”

zhParas: 夏威夷珍珠港-希卡姆联合基地——在Virginia-class潜艇注满水的压载水舱内，那里没有自然光，空间比肩宽还窄，澳大利亚皇家海军潜水员正在学习如何保障世界上最先进的水下平台之一。尽管这项工作艰苦、技术性强且令人幽闭，但它代表着迄今最明确的迹象之一：澳大利亚、美国和英国之间的增强型安全伙伴关系——奥库斯联盟——正在取得进展并交付成果。
“作为首批在美国接受这项训练、以便回澳大利亚形成新能力的潜水员之一，真的非常令人兴奋，”澳大利亚皇家海军上尉坎托纳（Cantona*）说。“军队里通常有你的[标准操作程序]和体系架构，但在这里，我们本质上是在创造全新的东西，这非常独特且罕见。”
坎托纳是在珍珠港海军船厂与中级维修设施（PHNSY & IMF）完成为期五个月全浸入式轮训的八名澳大利亚潜水员之一。他们是首批接受培训、达到与美国水兵和船厂人员同等水平来维护美国核动力攻击潜艇的澳大利亚潜水员。他们的任务包括学习在澳大利亚对Virginia-class潜艇执行潜水员作业所需的技能。
“能来到这里是一种荣幸，”坎托纳在夏威夷训练期间说。“我们正在为未来部队奠定基础——一支能够让潜艇保持战备、在海上并从印度洋执行任务的部队。”
这项训练既对体力要求很高，也对技术极为严格。每名潜水员都完全融入美国海军潜水队，执行水下工作，包括压载水舱内部部件更换、鱼雷发射管检查、电传操纵系统检查和索具作业。他们还完成了辐射潜水员认证和船厂安全资质。
“我们把他们当作自己人，”PHNSY & IMF司令部潜水官、高级准尉迈克尔·塔夫特（Michael Tuft）说。“没有特殊待遇。他们编在我们队里，执行同样的潜水任务，参加同样的简报，做同样的作业后清理。他们完成得非常出色。”
塔夫特说，澳大利亚皇家海军潜水员被编成两人小组，直接分配到美国潜水小队，使他们立即接触到日常维护作业的节奏。虽然澳大利亚皇家海军的专业潜水单位——清雷潜水部门——对复杂水下任务并不陌生，但核潜艇维护带来了新的技术要求。
“你不能每次出故障就把潜艇送进干船坞，”塔夫特说。“很多工作——尤其是压载水舱内部——必须在水下完成。而且不是随便什么人都能做。你需要受过训练的潜水员，达到这种精度水平，并具备这种信任水平。”
信任是潜水群体以及更广泛的奥库斯联盟伙伴关系中反复出现的主题。在水下，容不得半点迟疑。“你身边的人就是你的后盾。你必须知道，一旦出问题，他们会在那里，”澳大利亚皇家海军一等水兵芬恩（Finn）说。“令人惊叹的是，美国团队从一开始就给予了我们这种信任——而我们也赢得了它。”
这种信任不仅对安全至关重要，对战略战备也必不可少。随着美国、英国和澳大利亚继续落实奥库斯联盟第一支柱，互操作性不再是一个未来目标——而是当前的要求。

过去一年里，澳大利亚潜水员在两次重大的奥库斯联盟潜艇维护期中展示了技能。首先是在2025年11月美国对USS Vermont（SSN 792）的维护期间，随后是在2026年2月英国对HMS Anson的维护期间。这两次维护期均在西澳大利亚的HMAS Stirling进行，支持澳大利亚建立核动力潜艇自主保障能力的长期目标，这是奥库斯联盟的一项关键要求。在今年年底之前，澳大利亚潜水员还将在美国海军下一次计划中的潜艇维护期再次获得展示技能的机会。

在2026年5月的奥库斯联盟国防部长会议上，战争部长皮特·赫格塞思（Pete Hegseth）、澳大利亚副总理兼国防部长理查德·马尔斯（Richard Marles）和英国国防大臣约翰·希利（John Healey）确认，奥库斯联盟第一支柱仍按计划推进。在联合声明中，国防部长们还宣布，最早于2027年建立潜艇轮换部队-西部（SRF-West）的关键里程碑正在实现。根据SRF-West，美国和英国核动力攻击潜艇将从HMAS Stirling进行轮换部署。作为SRF-West的一部分，澳大利亚维护人员——包括这些新近接受训练的澳大利亚皇家海军潜水员——将在维护活动中发挥越来越大的作用，并继续积累操作和保障本国攻击潜艇舰队所需的专业知识。
“这是SRF-West最重要的基石之一，”奥库斯联盟整合与采办项目办公室负责SRF-West的副主任伊丽莎白·托林（Elizabeth Tolin）说。“最终，大部分保障工作将由澳大利亚人完成。我们现在正按我们的标准训练他们，以便我们能够在世界任何地方自信地共同行动。”
帮助建立潜水员培训流程的托林表示，这项工作需要将PHNSY & IMF转变为国际培训场所，这在海军造船厂中尚属首次。此前被指定为SRF-West牵头维护机构的PHNSY & IMF将在西澳大利亚设立维护分队，那里的美国维护人员将继续与澳大利亚同行并肩工作。
“我们必须先建立整套机制——课程、系统和政策——然后才能让学员下水，”托林说。“你现在看到的是一个合作伙伴正以速度和精准度挺身而出。”
这种伙伴关系不仅建立在共同价值观之上，也建立在作战必要性之上。
“嗯，如果潜艇出了故障，并不总能返回夏威夷，”塔夫特（Tuft）说。“如果它们位于澳大利亚附近，就可以驶入那里；而且我们知道，我们已经按照与美国相同的标准训练了澳大利亚人。他们能修好那艘潜艇，并让它重返前线。”
“SRF-West是奥库斯联盟第一支柱的基石，”奥库斯、国际与系统主任Rear Adm. 道格·亚当斯（Doug Adams）说。“对美国海军而言，从HMAS Stirling进行轮换部署可缩短航渡时间，增强攻击型潜艇的存在，并在印太地区以实力促和平。在澳大利亚建立维护能力，将使我们的潜艇保持随时能战，并为澳大利亚皇家海军及其保障伙伴今后维护自己的常规武装核动力潜艇舰队做好准备。”
据塔夫特称，这种培训正在印太地区打造一支灵活且有韧性的劳动力队伍。
“如果我们不堪重负，可以打电话给[澳大利亚人]说，‘嘿，能派六个人来吗？’他们也可以同样找我们。这就是我们正在建立的伙伴关系。我们可以在一切方面相互支持。”
对澳大利亚潜水员来说，这段经历既具职业意义，也同样具有个人意义。
“在潜艇压载水舱内潜水，肩膀紧贴舱壁，毫无能见度——这会让人心跳加速，”芬恩（Finn）说。“但能获得这些技能，并从第一天起帮助建立如此重要的事业，是莫大的荣幸。”
塔夫特说，该项目之外很少有人了解正在建设的这项工程规模有多大。
“这是我们最早开始培训外国伙伴维护我方潜艇的情形之一，”他说。“这充分说明了我们联盟的实力，以及我们多么信任澳大利亚人来帮助将其推向前进。”
随着潜水员准备返回澳大利亚并支援未来的潜艇维护周期，坎托纳（Cantona）表示，最重要的工作可能还在后头。
“我们需要改写一些政策，更新训练手册，建设基础设施，以便把在这里学到的东西推广开来，”他说。“但我们已经为此做好准备。我们得到了支持，我们掌握了知识。现在，我们要把它变成我们自己的东西。”
按照澳大利亚皇家海军的安全规程，只公布这名水兵的名。
