items.title: Bridging The Gap: Marines Test Emerging Technology for Southern Border Patrols
items.author: 2LT Louis Sosa
items.summary: U.S. Marines assigned to Joint Task Force-Southern Border, in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard, are testing emerging command-and-control (C2) capabilities designed to improve communications and situational awareness for mounted and dismounted patrols operating in remote environments along the southern border.
items.body:
SAN DIEGO — U.S. Marines assigned to Joint Task Force-Southern Border, in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard, are testing emerging command-and-control (C2) capabilities designed to improve communications and situational awareness for mounted and dismounted patrols operating in remote environments along the southern border.

The effort brought together Marines from 1st Battalion, 7th Marine Regiment, 1st Marine Division, and Combat Logistics Regiment 17 (CLR-17), 1st Marine Logistics Group (1st MLG), to address communications gaps encountered during operations. Together, they developed an innovative solution to overcome dead zones, restore connectivity in challenging terrain, and enhance small unmanned aerial systems (sUAS) already critical to patrol operations. This capability extends Marines’ visibility in mountainous terrain, allowing them to observe areas beyond ground-level line of sight while sharing a live video feed with dispersed ground troops.

Maintaining communications in mountainous terrain is a persistent challenge. Steep mountains and deep valleys can obstruct line-of-sight communications and severely degrade radio performance.

“The initial issue to overcome was radio communications in dead zones,” said Master Sgt. Steven Baez, a communications chief with CLR-17, 1st MLG. “These gaps in connectivity can limit the ability of patrols and units to maintain reliable communications and access critical information while operating in the field.”

To overcome the initial issue, the Marines started at the root problem: 5G dead zones. Maj. Michael Calnan, the regimental communications officer with CLR-17, 1st MLG, described how the team solved this problem.

“The most scalable solution was to push existing services into those dead zones, giving service members the tools they need to be effective,” said Calnan. “This solution was especially efficient because these systems are widely available as both government and commercial off-the-shelf solutions. This allowed the unit to experiment with emerging technology and develop individual solutions for each location based on requirements and needs.”

From Aug. 3–7, 2026, the Marines went out to several known dead zones within the San Diego Sector to test their concept.

“The goal of the demonstration was to integrate three separate capabilities into a single, more robust command-and-control solution,” said Baez. “By combining resilient tactical communications, live sUAS video feeds, and AI-enabled situational awareness, the objective was to enhance the ability of personnel to monitor and secure the border.”

The test leveraged Mobile Ad hoc Network (MANET) radios to build an adaptable meshed network that enabled all connected radios to communicate with one another where traditional signals fail.

“As nodes are added to a meshed network, it gets faster and more effective. This capability lets every connected radio talk to all others, regardless of terrain or other communication obstacles,” said Calnan.

With a MANET established, sUAS operators launched the Stalker VXE30 and Skydio X10 in areas where they were previously unable to fly. Once a reliable network was established and drones were flying above, the Marines pushed the live drone feed to Android Tactical Assault Kit (ATAK) devices. This integration solved a major tactical hurdle by bridging the gap between sUAS assets and ground-level tactical networks within the identified dead zones.

“The key technical breakthrough was establishing a complete command-and-control chain connecting the Starshield terminal, laptop, Compass service, and sUAS, and then transmitting the information to the tactical users on the ground,” said Baez.

With the Marines now able to view live feeds from sUAS assets on a portable ATAK device, another step of innovation presented itself: an artificial intelligence overlay that assists Marines by enhancing their current detection and monitoring capabilities. The overlay provides faster target recognition to identify individuals, vehicles, and other items, which can be configured to the needs of the patrol.

Following the successful demonstration, communications Marines are now focused on expanding the capability to a wider portion of the border mission. The next phase is aimed at reducing communication dead zones and increasing patrol access to live UAS feeds, real-time information, and AI-assisted identification capabilities to improve situational awareness.

For the individual Marine on patrol, this proof-of-concept translates to simplicity and speed of unique military capabilities brought to the southern border mission. Rather than managing multiple disconnected systems, a Marine can enhance situational awareness by viewing live aerial videos, receiving AI-aided alerts, and maintaining constant contact with headquarters. This streamlining significantly boosts operational speed and decision-making at the lowest level, while keeping higher headquarters involved.

U.S. Northern Command works side-by-side with the Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Customs and Border Protection within narrowly defined authorities to provide unique military capabilities to protect the territorial integrity of the southern border.
zhParas: 圣迭戈——配属给南部边境联合特遣部队、支援“热情先锋”行动的美国海军陆战队员，正在测试新兴指挥与控制（C2）能力，这些能力旨在改善在南部边境偏远环境中执行任务的乘车和徒步巡逻队的通信与态势感知。

这项工作汇集了来自海军陆战队第1师第7陆战团第1营以及海军陆战队第1后勤大队（1st MLG）第17战斗后勤团（CLR-17）的海军陆战队员，以解决行动中遇到的通信缺口。他们共同开发了一种创新解决方案，以克服盲区、在复杂地形中恢复连通性，并增强对巡逻行动已至关重要的小型无人机系统（sUAS）。该能力扩展了海军陆战队员在山地地形中的视野，使他们能够观察地面视距以外的区域，同时与分散的地面部队共享实时视频画面。
在山地地形中保持通信是一项长期挑战。陡峭的山脉和深谷会阻挡视距通信，并严重降低无线电性能。
“最初需要解决的问题是盲区中的无线电通信，”海军陆战队第1后勤大队（1st MLG）第17战斗后勤团（CLR-17）通信主管 Master Sgt. 史蒂文·贝兹（Steven Baez）说，“这些连通性缺口会限制巡逻队和部队在野外行动时保持可靠通信并获取关键信息的能力。”
为克服最初的问题，海军陆战队员从根源入手：5G盲区。海军陆战队第1后勤大队（1st MLG）第17战斗后勤团（CLR-17）团通信官 Maj. 迈克尔·卡尔南（Michael Calnan）描述了该团队如何解决这一问题。
“最具可扩展性的解决方案是将现有服务推入这些盲区，为军人提供发挥作用所需的工具，”卡尔南说，“这一解决方案尤其高效，因为这些系统作为政府和商业现成解决方案均可广泛获得。这使该部队能够试验新兴技术，并根据需求和需要为每个地点制定单独解决方案。”
2026年8月3日至7日，海军陆战队员前往圣迭戈防区内多个已知盲区测试其构想。
“此次演示的目标是将三种独立能力整合为一个更强大的单一指挥与控制解决方案，”贝兹说，“通过结合韧性战术通信、sUAS实时视频画面和人工智能赋能的态势感知，目标是增强人员监视和保卫边境的能力。”
此次测试利用移动自组网（MANET）电台构建了一个可自适应的网状网络，使所有已连接的电台在传统信号失效的地方能够彼此通信。
“随着节点加入网状网络，网络会变得更快、更有效。这种能力使每一部已连接的电台都能与所有其他电台通话，无论地形或其他通信障碍如何，”卡尔南（Calnan）说。
在建立MANET后，小型无人机系统（sUAS）操作员在以往无法飞行的区域发射了Stalker VXE30和Skydio X10。一旦建立起可靠网络且无人机在空中飞行，海军陆战队员便将无人机实时画面推送至Android Tactical Assault Kit（ATAK）设备。这一整合弥合了sUAS资产与已识别盲区内地面战术网络之间的差距，解决了重大战术障碍。
“关键的技术突破是建立了一条完整的指挥控制链，将Starshield终端、笔记本电脑、Compass服务和sUAS连接起来，然后将信息传输给地面战术用户，”贝兹（Baez）说。
由于海军陆战队员现在能够在便携式ATAK设备上查看sUAS资产的实时画面，另一项创新随之出现：一种人工智能叠加层，通过增强其现有探测与监视能力来协助海军陆战队员。该叠加层提供更快的目标识别，以识别人员、车辆和其他物品，并可根据巡逻需求进行配置。
在成功演示之后，通信专业的海军陆战队员现在专注于将该能力扩展至边境任务的更大范围。下一阶段旨在减少通信盲区，并增加巡逻队获取无人机系统实时画面、实时信息和人工智能辅助识别能力的机会，以提高态势感知能力。
对于巡逻中的海军陆战队员个人而言，这一概念验证意味着将独特军事能力以简便、快速的方式带到南部边境任务中。海军陆战队员无需管理多个互不连通的系统，而是可以通过观看实时空中视频、接收人工智能辅助警报以及与总部保持持续联系来增强态势感知。这种精简显著提升了最低层级的行动速度和决策能力，同时让上级总部保持参与。
美军北方司令部与国土安全部和美国海关与边境保护局在严格界定的权限范围内并肩合作，提供独特军事能力，以保护南部边境的领土完整。

items.title: CENTCOM Completes Exercise Eager Lion in Colorado
items.author: Courtesy
items.summary: CENTCOM Completes Exercise Eager Lion in Colorado
items.body:
COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. — U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) concluded Exercise Eager Lion 2026 on Sept. 24 at Fort Carson, Colorado. The two-week exercise included more than 200 military personnel from Jordan and the United States.

In the interview below, Brig. Gen. Mohammed Al-Maqdadi from the Jordanian Armed Forces (JAF) and U.S. Army Brig. Gen. William DiProfio from the Colorado Army National Guard discuss what the exercise accomplished.

Q: The State Partnership Program between Jordan and the Colorado National Guard has spanned over 22 years. How did training in Colorado strengthen the personal and professional bonds built over time?

Brig. Gen. Al-Maqdadi: Training directly with our counterparts here in Colorado strengthens our relationship by turning longstanding professional ties into practical, personal connections. Over more than 22 years, the State Partnership Program has created a strong foundation of trust and mutual understanding between the Jordanian Armed Forces - Arab Army and the Colorado National Guard. Training together allows us to exchange experience, understand each other's procedures, and build the professional relationships that are essential for effective cooperation.

Q: This was the 12th iteration of Eager Lion but the first hosted on U.S. soil, what has been the strategic value and operational advantage of bringing this bilateral training to Fort Carson, particularly for joint command post and cyber defense training?

Brig. Gen. DiProfio: Bringing Eager Lion to the United States for the first time demonstrates the strength and maturity of our relationship with the Jordanian Armed Forces. Training here at Fort Carson gave us an opportunity to operate together in a different environment and strengthen our ability to plan, communicate, and make decisions as a combined team. Whether we were working through command post operations, cyber defense, or disaster response, the value was enhancing interoperability. Every time we train together, solve problems together, and learn from one another, we strengthen the trust and readiness necessary to respond together when it matters.

Q: Jordan has a long history of hosting U.S. forces for Eager Lion. How did this reciprocal hosting enhance the mutual respect and camaraderie between forces?

Brig. Gen. Al-Maqdadi: Reciprocal hosting was a clear reflection of the depth of the Jordan-U.S. defense relationship. Jordan has welcomed U.S. forces to Eager Lion for many years, and conducting this exercise here in Colorado gave our forces the opportunity to experience each other's operating environments firsthand. This exchange strengthened mutual respect, built strong professional relationships, and reinforced our understanding that our partnership is based not only on training together, but also on shared professionalism, trust, and commitment.

Q: How did hosting Jordanian partners here in Colorado enhance overall total-force integration, especially with the active involvement of the Colorado and Illinois National Guard alongside active-duty personnel?

Brig. Gen. DiProfio: Eager Lion was a great example of the Total Force in action. It brought together active-duty personnel, National Guard members and our Jordanian partners around common training objectives. Colorado and Jordan have been partners in the State Partnership Program since 2004, and that relationship has been built through more than 500 military-to-military engagements. Bringing all of these organizations together at Fort Carson allowed us to build on that foundation, learn from one another, strengthen interoperability, and ultimately make each of our forces better prepared.

Q: Looking to the future, how does the success of this U.S.-hosted Eager Lion set a new benchmark for how forces will continue to adapt, innovate, and stand together against modern security challenges like cyber threats?

Brig. Gen. Al-Maqdadi: The success of a U.S.-hosted Eager Lion demonstrated our ability to adapt our cooperation at all levels. It gave our forces an opportunity to train across different domains, exchange expertise, and develop common approaches to emerging challenges, including cyber threats and counter terrorism and drug trafficking. Looking ahead, this experience provides a strong foundation for continued innovation, interoperability, and readiness while reinforcing the commitment of the Jordanian Armed Forces - Arab Army and U.S. forces to stand together.
zhParas: 科罗拉多州科罗拉多斯普林斯——美军中央司令部（CENTCOM）于9月24日在科罗拉多州卡森堡结束了“Eager Lion 2026”演习。这场为期两周的演习有来自约旦和美国的200多名军人参加。
在下面的采访中，约旦武装部队（JAF）的Brig. Gen.穆罕默德·马格达迪（Mohammed Al-Maqdadi）和来自科罗拉多陆军国民警卫队的美国陆军Brig. Gen.威廉·迪普罗菲奥（William DiProfio）讨论了此次演习取得的成果。
问：约旦与科罗拉多国民警卫队之间的州伙伴关系计划已持续超过22年。在科罗拉多的训练如何加强了多年来建立的个人与职业纽带？
Brig. Gen.马格达迪：在科罗拉多与我们的同行直接训练，将长期的专业联系转化为实际的个人联系，从而加强了我们的关系。22年多来，州伙伴关系计划在约旦武装部队—阿拉伯军与科罗拉多国民警卫队之间建立了牢固的信任与相互理解基础。共同训练使我们能够交流经验、了解彼此的程序，并建立对有效合作至关重要的职业关系。
问：这是“Eager Lion”演习的第12次举行，但却是首次在美国本土主办。将这一双边训练带到卡森堡，其战略价值和作战优势体现在哪里，尤其是对联合指挥所和网络防御训练而言？
Brig. Gen.迪普罗菲奥：将“Eager Lion”演习首次带到美国，体现了我们与约旦武装部队关系的牢固与成熟。在卡森堡的训练让我们有机会在不同环境中共同行动，并增强我们作为一个联合团队进行规划、沟通和决策的能力。无论是演练指挥所行动、网络防御还是灾害响应，其价值都在于提升互操作性。每当我们共同训练、共同解决问题、相互学习时，我们都在加强在关键时刻共同应对所需的信任与战备。
问：约旦长期以来一直承办美军参加的“Eager Lion”演习。这种对等互办的方式如何增进了两军之间的相互尊重和战友情谊？
Brig. Gen.马格达迪：互办演习清楚地反映了约旦—美国防务关系的深度。多年来，约旦一直欢迎美军参加“Eager Lion”演习，而在科罗拉多举行此次演习，让我军有机会亲身感受彼此的行动环境。这种交流增进了相互尊重，建立了牢固的职业关系，并加深了我们的认识：我们的伙伴关系不仅建立在共同训练之上，也建立在共同的职业精神、信任和承诺之上。
问：在科罗拉多州当地接待约旦伙伴，尤其是在科罗拉多州和伊利诺伊州国民警卫队与现役人员共同积极参与的情况下，如何增强了总体力量的整体整合？

Brig. Gen. 迪普罗菲奥（DiProfio）：Eager Lion 是总体力量付诸行动的一个绝佳范例。它围绕共同训练目标，将现役人员、国民警卫队成员和我们的约旦伙伴汇聚在一起。科罗拉多州和约旦自2004年以来一直是州伙伴关系计划中的伙伴，这一关系通过500多次军队对军队交流建立起来。将这些组织齐聚卡森堡，使我们能够在此基础上继续发展、相互学习、加强互操作性，并最终使我们每一支部队都准备得更充分。
问：展望未来，美国主办的 Eager Lion 取得的成功，如何为部队今后继续适应、创新并团结一致应对网络威胁等现代安全挑战树立新的标杆？
Brig. Gen. 阿尔-马格达迪（Al-Maqdadi）：美国主办的 Eager Lion 的成功，展示了我们在各个层面调整合作的能力。它使我们的部队有机会进行跨域训练、交流专长，并针对包括网络威胁、反恐和毒品贩运在内的新兴挑战制定共同办法。展望未来，这一经验为持续创新、互操作性和战备提供了坚实基础，同时强化了约旦武装部队—阿拉伯军与美军团结一致的承诺。

items.title: Arnold AFB Airmen participate in mask fit validation
items.author: Bradley Hicks
items.summary: A different type of testing is in progress at Arnold Air Force Base. The latest effort does not involve propulsion or aerodynamics. Instead, validation testing is ongoing for all military personnel at Arnold, headquarters of Arnold Engineering Development Complex, to ensure protective masks fit and seal properly.
items.body: ARNOLD AIR FORCE BASE, Tenn. – A different type of testing is in progress at Arnold Air Force Base. The latest effort does not involve propulsion or aerodynamics. Instead, validation testing is ongoing for all military personnel at Arnold, headquarters of Arnold Engineering Development Complex, to ensure protective masks fit and seal properly. “Upon appointing two certified Mask Fit Validation Monitors, mask fit validation testing is officially underway within AEDC,” said AEDC Chief of Logistics and Health Services William Russell. “Administering these validation tests is paramount to ensuring every Airman adheres to grooming standards and maintains operational survivability in hazardous environments by undergoing a visible protective mask seal test.” The mask testing, which began Sept. 22 at Arnold, is being conducted to comply with Tasking Order 26-39, a Department of the Air Force directive mandating that all Airmen complete gas mask seal tests. This order reinforces the Secretary of War’s guidance titled “Grooming Standards for Facial Hair Implementation,” which dictates that all tight-fitting respiratory equipment requires an unobstructed, clean-shaven seal surface to function effectively. “A protective mask offers virtually no defense against lethal airborne pathogens, toxic industrial chemicals, or [Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear] agents if facial hair compromises skin-to-mask interface,” Russell added. “By strictly integrating the SECWAR grooming standards with the physical negative-pressure seal checks executed by the new validation monitors, AEDC ensures that medical shaving waivers and accommodations do not interfere with warfighter safety.” Testing is performed in-person using the M50 Gas Mask, the standard deployment gas mask. The test involves a negative-pressure verification. Essentially, each Airmen puts on the mask and a check in performed to ensure the mask fits snugly and functions without air leaks. “Members will don the M50 Gas Mask then conduct a negative-pressure check,” said Tech. Sgt. Gregory Rollings, a Mask Fit Validation Monitor, or MFVM, at Arnold AFB. “Using both hands, the member will cover the M61 filter air inlet passages on both filters and breathe in. The mask should collapse inwards toward the face and remain so as they hold the in-breath. “If the mask stays collapsed inward with no air leaks, then it is considered airtight. If the mask does not maintain negative pressure, they are checked for hair, clothing or improper size and then retested. If the member fails three times, they will be marked as non-compliant.” If an Airman is found to be in non-compliance, his or her commander is notified via a memorandum, Rollings said. Mask fit testing must be completed by Dec. 31, and all military personnel, regardless of gender, must be validated. Rollings and Tech Sgt. Derek Gould, his alternate MFVM, will reach out to Arnold military personnel who have not yet been validated to ensure all are in compliance by the end of the year. “Ultimately, enforcing these rigorous standards safeguards the installation’s warfighters, ensuring that personnel remain lethal, compliant and fully capable of executing national security objectives when called upon to deploy,” Russell said.

Sgt. 格雷戈里·罗林斯（Gregory Rollings）说。“人员将用双手遮住两个M61滤毒罐上的进气通道，并吸气。面具应向面部内陷，并在其屏住吸气时保持内陷状态。如果面具保持向内凹陷且无漏气，则视为气密。如果面具未能保持负压，则检查其是否有毛发、衣物或尺寸不当，然后重新测试。如果该人员三次未通过，将被标记为不合规。”罗林斯说，如果发现空军人员不合规，将通过备忘录通知其指挥官。面具适配测试必须在12月31日前完成，所有军事人员无论性别都必须接受验证。罗林斯和Tech Sgt. 德里克·古尔德（Derek Gould）——他的候补MFVM——将联系尚未接受验证的阿诺德基地军事人员，以确保所有人在年底前合规。“最终，执行这些严格标准可保护该基地的作战人员，确保人员保持杀伤力、合规性，并在被要求部署时完全有能力执行国家安全目标，”拉塞尔说。

items.title: US appeals court upholds Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: A federal appeals court upheld the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic from military contracts, handing a victory to President Trump and the Pentagon.
items.body:
A federal appeals court on Friday upheld the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic from military contracts, handing a victory to President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in their battle with the AI startup over safety guardrails on its technology.

The 2-1 decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals in Washington came in a lawsuit by Anthropic challenging its March designation by the Pentagon as a national security supply chain risk, which the startup says has cost it billions of dollars in lost business and damaged its reputation ahead of a highly anticipated initial public offering.

The court’s majority said it was reasonable for the Pentagon to designate Anthropic after it refused to allow its products to be used for autonomous weapons or mass surveillance. It rejected Anthropic’s claim that the Pentagon had retaliated against it for its views on AI safety and ethics.

Siding with Hegseth’s argument that Anthropic’s safety restrictions could compromise military operations, the majority said, “The Secretary raises the deeply sobering prospect of overly constrained AI models shutting down unexpectedly and thus causing important military operations to fail,” in an opinion by Judge Gregory Katsas.

San Francisco-based Anthropic said in a statement Friday that it respectfully disagrees with the decision but remains confident in its position and is considering its options, including review of the three-judge panel’s decision by the full appeals court.

The White House and the Department of Defense did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.

A federal judge in San Francisco last month struck down a parallel designation under a different law, finding the administration had unlawfully retaliated against Anthropic for its views on AI safety. U.S. District Judge Rita Lin in San Francisco also blocked Trump’s government-wide ban on Anthropic and Hegseth’s order barring military contractors from doing any business with the startup.

Hegseth designated Anthropic as a risk under two different laws after Anthropic refused to remove guardrails against its technology being used for autonomous weapons or mass domestic surveillance.

The unprecedented move came after months of negotiations ended in failure and public recriminations by Hegseth and Trump, who accused Anthropic of endangering American lives with ideological posturing.

Anthropic denied that characterization and said AI is not yet reliable enough to be safely used in autonomous weapons. The company also said it opposes domestic surveillance as a violation of fundamental rights.
zhParas: 周五，一家联邦上诉法院维持了五角大楼将Anthropic列入军事合同黑名单的决定，这使总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)和国防部长皮特·海格塞斯(Pete Hegseth)在与这家AI初创公司就其技术安全护栏的争斗中获胜。
华盛顿的美国联邦上诉法院以2比1作出的这一裁决，源于Anthropic提起的诉讼，该公司质疑五角大楼在3月将其指定为国家安全供应链风险。这家初创公司称，这一指定使其损失了数十亿美元业务，并在备受期待的首次公开募股前损害了其声誉。
法院多数意见称，在Anthropic拒绝允许其产品被用于自主武器或大规模监控后，五角大楼将其指定为风险是合理的。法院驳回了Anthropic的说法，即五角大楼因其在AI安全与伦理方面的观点而对其实施报复。
多数意见支持海格塞斯的论点，即Anthropic的安全限制可能危及军事行动。在法官格雷戈里·卡察斯(Gregory Katsas)撰写的一份意见书中，多数意见称：“部长提出了一个令人深感警醒的前景：受到过度约束的AI模型意外关闭，从而导致重要军事行动失败。”
总部位于旧金山的Anthropic周五在一份声明中表示，它尊重但不同意该裁决，但对其立场仍抱有信心，并正在考虑各种选项，包括由全体上诉法院法官复审该三人法官合议庭的裁决。
白宫和国防部没有立即回应寻求置评的电子邮件。
上月，旧金山的一名联邦法官推翻了依据另一部法律作出的类似指定，认定政府因Anthropic在AI安全方面的观点而对其实施了非法报复。旧金山的美国地区法官丽塔·林(Rita Lin)还阻止了特朗普针对Anthropic的整个政府范围的禁令，以及海格塞斯禁止军事承包商与该初创公司开展任何业务的命令。
在Anthropic拒绝移除防止其技术被用于自主武器或大规模国内监控的护栏后，海格塞斯依据两部不同法律将其指定为风险。
这一史无前例的举动出台之前，长达数月的谈判以失败告终，赫格塞思（Hegseth）与特朗普还公开互相指责，他们指控Anthropic以意识形态作秀，危及美国人的生命。
Anthropic否认这一说法，并表示人工智能目前尚不够可靠，无法安全地用于自主武器。该公司还表示，反对国内监控，认为这侵犯了基本权利。

items.title: Hungary, Ohio state partners discuss accomplishments, future plans during annual capstone visit
items.author: SSgt Nicholas Battani
items.summary: The Ohio National Guard’s 33-yearlong partnership with Hungary was on full display during an annual capstone visit in summer 2026, as part of the ongoing National Guard State Partnership Program. items.body:
The Ohio National Guard’s 33-yearlong partnership with Hungary was on full display during an annual capstone visit this summer, as part of the ongoing National Guard State Partnership Program.

Maj. Gen. Matthew S. Woodruff, Ohio adjutant general, led a delegation to meet with Hungarian Defence Forces officials to highlight the past year’s SPP exchanges and plan for future events. He also observed Exercise Neighbors, an annual multinational training event that showcased the interoperability and strength of the partnerships Ohio has built with both the Hungarian Defence Forces and Serbian Armed Forces.

“The most significant part of us participating in exercises like Neighbors is we get to work together with two of our state partners — not just Hungary, but Serbia,” Woodruff said. “We come together and conduct an amazing event where three different countries are working together to show the strength that comes when we all work together as a team.”

The exercise culminated in a complex trench-clearing operation involving service members from all three nations. Despite language differences and varying military backgrounds, participating forces successfully coordinated their efforts to accomplish the mission.

“A trench mission is one of the most complex things we do,” Woodruff said. “To have three different countries that sometimes have a language barrier work together, train together and accomplish the objective shows how effective these partnerships have become.”

The training scenario reflected lessons learned from current conflicts around the world. Woodruff noted that military planners continue adapting training exercises to prepare troops for evolving battlefield conditions.

“If you look at the Ukraine-Russia war, trench warfare is something we haven’t seen for years. We must take those lessons learned and implement them into current training plans to ensure our Soldiers, the Hungarian Defence Forces and the Serbian Armed Forces are prepared to operate in the most challenging and dynamic environments.”

While emerging technologies such as drones continue to reshape modern warfare, Woodruff stressed that traditional ground forces remain essential.

“Drones are an important part of warfare now, and we’re seeing that in conflicts around the world,” he said. “But you can never hold and maintain ground without infantry on the ground. It’s going to be a combination of both drone technology and the infantry Soldier.”

Beyond the field training, Woodruff met with senior Hungarian military leaders to discuss future opportunities for cooperation. During meetings with Hungarian Defence Forces leadership, discussions focused on expanding collaboration in areas such as cyber operations, air defense and military decision-making processes.

“We talked about future opportunities for the Hungarian Defence Forces and the Ohio National Guard,” Woodruff said. “These are still in the early stages, but they’re exciting opportunities to continue expanding our partnership.”

The Ohio National Guard and Hungary have maintained a partnership through the State Partnership Program since 1993, making it one of the program’s longest-standing relationships. Ohio’s partnership with Serbia began in 2006 and has continued to grow through recurring exchanges, exercises and leadership engagements. Ohio’s third state partnership — with the Republic of Angola — was formalized this year, beginning a new era of exchanges techniques, tactics and procedures, growing capabilities and building relationships to support regional stability and shared security objectives.

Woodruff said the enduring relationships formed through the SPP remain one of its greatest strengths.

“This trip has been amazing for all of us,” he said. “From the Soldier level, executing missions alongside Hungarian and Serbian partners, to leadership engagements across the Hungarian Defence Forces, these relationships are what make us strong. The partnership that’s been 33 years with Hungary and 20 years with Serbia is what makes us strong.”

Woodruff reflected on how leadership engagements and shared training opportunities like Exercise Neighbors continue to strengthen all three nations.

“Every time we get together and engage at the leadership level, it develops opportunities for us to find new paths to continue growing as an Ohio National Guard and as partners with Hungary,” he said. “Each time we train together, our Soldiers become stronger, and hopefully our Hungarian partners walk away feeling they have improved as well.”

The State Partnership Program continues to serve as a cornerstone of international military cooperation, fostering professional relationships, enhancing readiness and strengthening security partnerships that extend far beyond the training field.
zhParas: 俄亥俄国民警卫队与匈牙利长达33年的伙伴关系，在今年夏天的一次年度压轴访问中得到充分展示，这是正在进行的国民警卫队州伙伴关系计划的一部分。
俄亥俄州副官长 Maj. Gen. 马修·S·伍德拉夫（Matthew S. Woodruff）率领代表团会见了匈牙利国防军官员，以重点展示过去一年的州伙伴关系计划交流并规划未来活动。他还观摩了“Neighbors”演习，这是一项年度多国训练活动，展示了俄亥俄州与匈牙利国防军和塞尔维亚武装力量建立的伙伴关系的互操作性与实力。
“我们参加像‘Neighbors’这样的演习，最重要的部分是我们能与两个州伙伴——不仅是匈牙利，还有塞尔维亚——一起合作，”伍德拉夫说。“我们聚在一起，举办一场了不起的活动，三个不同国家共同努力，展示当我们作为一个团队合作时所产生的力量。”
演习最终以一场复杂的堑壕清理行动告终，来自三国的军人参与其中。尽管存在语言差异和不同的军事背景，参演部队仍成功协调行动，完成了任务。
“堑壕任务是我们执行的最复杂任务之一，”伍德拉夫说。“让三个有时存在语言障碍的不同国家一起合作、一起训练并完成目标，表明这些伙伴关系已经变得多么有效。”
训练想定反映了从当今世界冲突中吸取的经验教训。伍德拉夫指出，军事规划人员继续调整训练演习，以使部队为不断变化的战场条件做好准备。
“如果你看看乌克兰-俄罗斯战争，堑壕战是我们多年未见的东西。我们必须吸取这些经验教训，并将其落实到当前训练计划中，以确保我们的士兵、匈牙利国防军和塞尔维亚武装力量准备好能够在最具挑战性和动态的环境中行动。”
尽管无人机等新兴技术继续重塑现代战争，伍德拉夫强调传统地面部队仍然不可或缺。
“无人机现在是战争的重要组成部分，我们在世界各地的冲突中都看到了这一点，”他说。“但如果没有地面上的步兵，你永远无法守住和维持阵地。这将是无人机技术与步兵士兵的结合。”
除实地训练外，伍德拉夫（Woodruff）还会见了匈牙利高级军事领导人，讨论未来合作机会。在与匈牙利国防军领导层的会晤中，讨论重点是在网络行动、防空和军事决策流程等领域扩大合作。
“我们讨论了匈牙利国防军和俄亥俄州国民警卫队未来的机会，”伍德拉夫说。“这些仍处于早期阶段，但它们是继续扩大我们伙伴关系的令人兴奋的机会。”
自1993年以来，俄亥俄州国民警卫队与匈牙利一直通过州伙伴关系计划保持伙伴关系，这使其成为该计划持续时间最长的关系之一。俄亥俄州与塞尔维亚的伙伴关系始于2006年，并通过定期交流、演习和领导层接触不断发展。俄亥俄州的第三个州伙伴关系——与安哥拉共和国——于今年正式确立，开启了一个交流技术、战术和程序、提升能力并建立关系以支持地区稳定和共同安全目标的新时代。
伍德拉夫说，通过州伙伴关系计划形成的持久关系仍是其最大优势之一。
“这次旅行对我们所有人来说都非常棒，”他说。“从士兵层面与匈牙利和塞尔维亚伙伴一起执行任务，到与匈牙利国防军各层面的领导层接触，这些关系使我们强大。与匈牙利长达33年、与塞尔维亚长达20年的伙伴关系，正是使我们强大的原因。”
伍德拉夫回顾了领导层接触和像“邻国演习”这样的共同训练机会如何继续加强这三个国家。
“每次我们聚在一起并在领导层面接触，都会为我们创造机会，找到新路径，继续作为俄亥俄州国民警卫队以及与匈牙利的伙伴发展壮大，”他说。“每次我们一起训练，我们的士兵都会变得更强，希望我们的匈牙利伙伴离开时也感到自己有所提高。”
州伙伴关系计划依然是国际军事合作的基石，它促进职业关系、提升战备水平，并加强远远超出训练场范畴的安全伙伴关系。

items.body:
JOINT BASE LANGLEY-EUSTIS, Va. — U.S. Army Capt. Austin Clark, 841st Transportation Battalion, 597th Transportation Brigade, ARTRANS, operations (S3) officer, completed the rigorous Rail Conductor Certification Course at Fort Eustis, Virginia, this month, becoming the only active-duty commissioned officer in the United States Army to hold the prestigious qualification. In an era where strategic mobility and contested logistics dictate combat power projection, rail deployment remains one of the military's most critical expeditionary capabilities.

The course was conducted by the Maritime and Intermodal Training Department, a component of the 71st Transportation Battalion at Joint Base Langley-Eustis. The department serves as the premier training engine for the Army’s multimodal logistics force, delivering critical institutional instruction across six distinct Transportation Corps military occupational specialties: cargo specialist (MOS 88H), watercraft operator (MOS 88K), watercraft engineer (MOS 88L), railway operations specialist (MOS 88U), marine deck officer (MOS 880A) and marine engineer officer (MOS 881A).

The railway operations specialist MOS is unique to the U.S. Army Reserve, providing specialized rail network capability, infrastructure assessments, host-nation and contracted rail planning, and contracting officer representative duties to oversee rail contracts. Trained at Fort Eustis as part of the Transportation School's distributed footprint, this capability represents a vital link in strategic mobility.

The U.S. Army Transportation School, headquartered at Fort Gregg-Adams, Virginia (formerly Fort Lee), operates as a geographically distributed One Army School System comprised of three separate training locations that prepare transportation professionals across all components—Active, Reserve and National Guard. Clark's achievement bridges that institutional framework with direct, tactical rail proficiency. Rail operations are the heavy-lift backbone of power projection, moving massive tonnage from fort to port with speed and efficiency.

As Col. Lillard D. Evans, former deputy commander for the Military Surface Deployment and Distribution Command (now ARTRANS), emphasized, "Our warfighting capability relies upon rail. The positive relationships we maintain with our commercial rail partners is key to our success in moving, deploying and sustaining the armed forces to deliver readiness at speed."

Anchoring this capability is the institutional mission of the U.S. Army Transportation School, which lives by the enduring operational tenet: "Nothing happens until something moves." Earning rail conductor certification isn't just a personal achievement—it ensures our active-duty officer corps maintains the technical depth required to plan, synchronize and execute intermodal rail movements in contested logistics environments.

When an armored brigade deploys, trains must be scheduled, sequenced and loaded at home station. When those railcars arrive at the port, that cargo must be safely marshaled, offloaded and balanced aboard ship with zero margin of error.

Clark’s achievement directly empowers the operational mission of the 841st Transportation Battalion. Headquartered at Joint Base Charleston, South Carolina, where the 841st serves as the single port manager responsible for Department of War surface cargo across commercial and military terminals spanning the Eastern Seaboard—from Maine to Florida—as well as Puerto Rico and the Caribbean basin.

Handling hundreds of railcars per day during major surge operations, the battalion routinely stages, discharges and loads armored divisions, artillery and combat aviation task forces arriving by rail directly onto strategic sealift vessels.

The Rail Conductor Certification demands exhaustive mastery of Federal Railroad Administration guidelines, safety protocols, air brake systems, locomotive mechanical operations, track warrant control and complex freight switching maneuvers.

While rail operations within the Army have historically relied heavily on specialized Reserve Component personnel, Clark’s certification injects vital technical expertise directly into the active-duty operational force.

By setting the standard on the rails at Fort Eustis, Clark exemplifies the forward-looking mindset required of modern Transportation Corps officers—mastering the technical details of intermodal operations to ensure combat units deploy rapidly and arrive ready to fight– every time, on time**.**
zhParas: 弗吉尼亚州兰利-尤斯蒂斯联合基地——美国陆军Capt.奥斯汀·克拉克（Austin Clark）是ARTRANS第597运输旅第841运输营的作战（S3）军官，本月他在弗吉尼亚州尤斯蒂斯堡完成了严格的铁路列车长认证课程，成为美国陆军中唯一拥有这一殊荣资格的现役委任军官。在战略机动与对抗性后勤决定战斗力投送的时代，铁路部署仍是军队最关键的远征能力之一。
该课程由兰利-尤斯蒂斯联合基地第71运输营下属的海运与多式联运训练部主办。该部是陆军多式联运后勤力量的首要训练机构，在运输兵六个不同的军事职业专业上提供关键的机构性教学：货物装卸专业兵（MOS 88H）、船艇操作员（MOS 88K）、船艇工程师（MOS 88L）、铁路运营专业兵（MOS 88U）、航海甲板军官（MOS 880A）和轮机军官（MOS 881A）。
铁路运营专业兵这一军事职业专业为美国陆军预备役所独有，提供专业化的铁路网能力、基础设施评估、东道国与合同铁路规划，以及监督铁路合同的合同官代表职责。该能力作为运输学校分布式布局的一部分在尤斯蒂斯堡训练，是战略机动中的关键一环。
美国陆军运输学校总部位于弗吉尼亚州格雷格-亚当斯堡（原李堡），以地域分布式的一体化陆军学校体系运作，由三个独立训练地点组成，为现役、预备役和国民警卫队各组成部分培养运输专业人才。克拉克的成就在这一机构框架与直接的战术铁路专业技能之间架起了桥梁。铁路运营是力量投送的重载骨干，以速度和效率将巨量物资从营区运往港口。
正如军事水面部署与配送司令部（现为ARTRANS）前副司令Col.利拉德·D·埃文斯（Lillard D. Evans）所强调的：“我们的作战能力依赖铁路。我们与商业铁路伙伴保持的良好关系，是我们成功运送、部署和保障武装部队、以速度交付战备的关键。”
支撑这一能力的是美国陆军运输学校的机构使命，其恪守的长期作战信条是：“没有物资流动，一切皆无从谈起。”获得铁路列车长认证不仅是个人成就——它确保我们现役军官队伍保持在对抗性后勤环境中规划、同步和执行多式联运铁路运输所需的技术深度。
当一个装甲旅部署时，列车必须在驻地完成调度、排序和装载。当这些铁路车辆抵达港口时，货物必须安全编组、卸载并在船上配载平衡，不容任何差错。
克拉克的成就直接增强了第841运输营的作战任务能力。该营总部设在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿联合基地，在此作为唯一的港口管理机构，负责战争部在从缅因州到佛罗里达州的东海岸沿线，以及波多黎各和加勒比海盆地的商用与军用码头的水面货物。
在重大激增行动期间，该营每天处理数百节铁路车皮，例行集结、卸载并装载经铁路抵达的装甲师、炮兵和战斗航空特遣部队，将其直接送上战略海运船。
铁路列车长认证要求全面精通联邦铁路管理局指南、安全规程、空气制动系统、机车机械操作、轨道许可控制以及复杂的货运调车操作。
尽管美国陆军的铁路运输业务历来严重依赖专业化的预备役部队人员，但克拉克（Clark）的认证将至关重要的技术专长直接注入现役作战部队。
通过在尤斯蒂斯堡的铁路工作中树立标准，克拉克展现了现代运输兵团军官所需的前瞻性思维——精通多式联运的技术细节，确保作战部队快速部署并抵达后即可投入战斗——每一次，准时。
items.zhFull:
弗吉尼亚州兰利-尤斯蒂斯联合基地——美国陆军Capt.奥斯汀·克拉克（Austin Clark）是ARTRANS第597运输旅第841运输营的作战（S3）军官，本月他在弗吉尼亚州尤斯蒂斯堡完成了严格的铁路列车长认证课程，成为美国陆军中唯一拥有这一殊荣资格的现役委任军官。在战略机动与对抗性后勤决定战斗力投送的时代，铁路部署仍是军队最关键的远征能力之一。

该课程由兰利-尤斯蒂斯联合基地第71运输营下属的海运与多式联运训练部主办。该部是陆军多式联运后勤力量的首要训练机构，在运输兵六个不同的军事职业专业上提供关键的机构性教学：货物装卸专业兵（MOS 88H）、船艇操作员（MOS 88K）、船艇工程师（MOS 88L）、铁路运营专业兵（MOS 88U）、航海甲板军官（MOS 880A）和轮机军官（MOS 881A）。

铁路运营专业兵这一军事职业专业为美国陆军预备役所独有，提供专业化的铁路网能力、基础设施评估、东道国与合同铁路规划，以及监督铁路合同的合同官代表职责。该能力作为运输学校分布式布局的一部分在尤斯蒂斯堡训练，是战略机动中的关键一环。

美国陆军运输学校总部位于弗吉尼亚州格雷格-亚当斯堡（原李堡），以地域分布式的一体化陆军学校体系运作，由三个独立训练地点组成，为现役、预备役和国民警卫队各组成部分培养运输专业人才。克拉克的成就在这一机构框架与直接的战术铁路专业技能之间架起了桥梁。铁路运营是力量投送的重载骨干，以速度和效率将巨量物资从营区运往港口。

正如军事水面部署与配送司令部（现为ARTRANS）前副司令Col.利拉德·D·埃文斯（Lillard D. Evans）所强调的：“我们的作战能力依赖铁路。我们与商业铁路伙伴保持的良好关系，是我们成功运送、部署和保障武装部队、以速度交付战备的关键。”

支撑这一能力的是美国陆军运输学校的机构使命，其恪守的长期作战信条是：“没有物资流动，一切皆无从谈起。”获得铁路列车长认证不仅是个人成就——它确保我们现役军官队伍保持在对抗性后勤环境中规划、同步和执行多式联运铁路运输所需的技术深度。

当一个装甲旅部署时，列车必须在驻地完成调度、排序和装载。当这些铁路车辆抵达港口时，货物必须安全编组、卸载并在船上配载平衡，不容任何差错。

克拉克的成就直接增强了第841运输营的作战任务能力。该营总部设在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿联合基地，在此作为唯一的港口管理机构，负责战争部在从缅因州到佛罗里达州的东海岸沿线，以及波多黎各和加勒比海盆地的商用与军用码头的水面货物。

在重大激增行动期间，该营每天处理数百节铁路车皮，例行集结、卸载并装载经铁路抵达的装甲师、炮兵和战斗航空特遣部队，将其直接送上战略海运船。

铁路列车长认证要求全面精通联邦铁路管理局指南、安全规程、空气制动系统、机车机械操作、轨道许可控制以及复杂的货运调车操作。

尽管美国陆军的铁路运输业务历来严重依赖专业化的预备役部队人员，但克拉克（Clark）的认证将至关重要的技术专长直接注入现役作战部队。

通过在尤斯蒂斯堡的铁路工作中树立标准，克拉克展现了现代运输兵团军官所需的前瞻性思维——精通多式联运的技术细节，确保作战部队快速部署并抵达后即可投入战斗——每一次，准时。

items.title: US Navy stands up hub to prepare unmanned systems for combat
items.author: Riley Ceder
items.summary: U.S. Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle announced a new autonomous development center to train sailors and test new technology.
items.body:
The U.S. Navy announced Thursday a new development center that will train sailors to use autonomous technology in preparation for robotic systems to deploy across the entire fleet.

The service established the Robot and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Center at Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek, Virginia, ushering in a new era that will teach service members to be technically proficient while developing and fielding new combat-ready robotic systems.

“A prototype is not combat power,” Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle said in a C-NOte message. “Combat power comes when a trained sailor can employ a reliable system, supported by the right networks, logistics, maintenance, software, tactics, authorities, and command relationships, to create an operational effect.”

The new center provides a place to work on autonomous system integration so that by the time sailors in the fleet get their hands on the technology, it is ready to be used.

RASWDC will first focus on training sailors at the center to understand the systems enough to employ them in combat, while developing a broader system for teaching that can be disseminated through the entire Navy to help service members learn the technology.

The center will help create warfighting concepts that delineate strict guidelines for how commanders build mission plans and set frameworks for autonomous systems to operate within. These guidelines become especially important when systems are forced to operate in combat environments where communication between robotic technology and the human in the loop is compromised.

RASWDC will also test emerging systems in environments that mimic those in which they will be deployed. Technology will be asked to perform at sea, under stress, against simulated threats and during degraded communication environments.

The systems that achieve their goal despite these obstacles will continue to be developed with the end goal of employing them on the battlefield, while others that fail will be retired.

Caudle defined the intended cycle as field, employ, learn, improve and scale.

Caudle released another C-NOte on Sept. 2, calling for the swift integration of lasers and their offensive capabilities into the fleet.

“The question is no longer whether these systems work — it is how quickly we can field them across the fleet and place them in the hands of sailors,” Caudle said.

On Tuesday, the Navy demonstrated a new information-sharing capability that allows it to streamline communication between operators and autonomous aircraft.

Riley Ceder is a Navy reporter at Military Times, where he covers issues directly affecting service members and their families, as well as breaking news.
zhParas: 美国海军周四宣布成立一个新的发展中心，将培训水兵使用自主技术，为机器人系统在全舰队范围内部署做好准备。
该军种在弗吉尼亚州利特尔克里克联合远征基地成立了机器人及自主系统作战发展中心，由此开启一个新时代：在培养军人技术精通能力的同时，研发并部署新型可投入作战的机器人系统。
“原型不等于战斗力，”海军作战部长 Adm. 达里尔·考德尔（Daryl Caudle）在一份 C-NOte 消息中表示。“战斗力来自一名受过训练的水兵能够运用可靠的系统，并得到合适的网络、后勤、维修、软件、战术、授权和指挥关系的支撑，从而产生作战效果。”
新中心提供了一个开展自主系统集成工作的场所，以便舰队水兵接触到相关技术时，该技术已经可以投入使用。
RASWDC 将首先专注于在该中心培训水兵，使其充分了解这些系统，从而能在战斗中使用它们，同时开发一套可在整个海军推广的、更广泛的教学体系，帮助军人学习相关技术。
该中心将协助制定作战概念，为指挥官如何制定任务计划划定严格准则，并为自主系统的运行设定框架。当系统被迫在机器人技术与在环人类之间通信受损的战斗环境中运行时，这些准则尤为重要。
RASWDC 还将在模拟其部署环境的场景中测试新兴系统。相关技术将被要求在海上、承受压力、面对模拟威胁以及通信降级的环境下运行。
在这些障碍下仍能达成目标的系统将继续研发，最终目标是将其用于战场；而未能通过考验的系统则将被淘汰。
考德尔（Caudle）将预期循环定义为：部署、运用、学习、改进和扩展。
9月2日，考德尔发布了另一份 C-NOte，呼吁将激光器及其进攻能力迅速集成到舰队中。
“问题不再是这些系统是否管用——而是我们多快能将它们部署到整个舰队，并交到水兵手中，”考德尔说。
周二，海军展示了一种新的信息共享能力，使其能够简化操作员与自主飞机之间的通信。
莱利·塞德（Riley Ceder）是《军事时报》（Military Times）的海军记者，负责报道直接影响军人及其家属的问题以及突发新闻。

items.title: Thales in ‘quite advanced’ talks with NATO countries on AI-powered command software
items.author: Rudy Ruitenberg
items.summary: French firm Thales is “quite advanced” in discussions with a number of NATO countries about using its artificial intelligence-powered C2 system.
items.body:
PARIS — French defense-technology firm Thales is “quite advanced” in discussions with a number of NATO countries about using its artificial intelligence-powered command-and-control system HexaForce, said the company’s vice president for multi-domain operations, Patrick Moreau.

Thales announced the availability of HexaForce last week, after testing it during NATO’s Coalition Warrior Interoperability Exercise, or CWIX, in Poland in June. The company is positioning the system as a multi-domain C2 “overlay” that can plug into legacy and national systems from the strategic to the tactical level, while allowing users to choose their own AI models and avoid vendor lock-in.

NATO is increasingly turning to AI to harness growing amounts of data in command and control, and already operates a C2 system supplied by United States-based Palantir Technologies. Meanwhile, the European Union is looking to accelerate development and deployment of European capabilities amid concern about sovereign control of the technology underpinning them.

“I don’t want to go too much into detail. but we are quite advanced in some discussions with some NATO countries so far,” Moreau told Defense News in a Sept. 24 interview.

As European and NATO militaries look to scale operations from brigade-level formations to army corps of more than 100,000 troops, AI will be key to processing more complex data, shortening planning cycles and improving situational awareness, Moreau said.

HexaForce is aimed at providing command and control from the army corps level down to the battalion, according to the executive. Thales defined a goal with end users to be able to plan 1,000 target missions a day, a tenfold increase.

The system has an open architecture built around NATO standards, allowing countries to plug in existing systems for tasks such as mission planning, or use the large language model of their choice, according to Moreau. In addition to the LLM component, HexaForce includes agentic AI for tasks such as targeting mission preparation.

It has a fully distributed architecture designed to rely on mesh capability, allowing the system to be spread over different data hubs within different command posts, in line with new operational concepts to not rely on central computing, according to Moreau.

By interfacing with legacy solutions, HexaForce can add “AI-powered capability” to systems already in use by the armed forces, according to Moreau. HexaForce is a command-and-control system, and users still need dedicated tactical systems to provide sensor data, he said.

The executive said the aim at CWIX was for end users to test HexaForce and its interoperability with existing and legacy systems. The system implements NATO standards related to the Data-Centric Security and Federation Mission Networking frameworks, he said.

For threats identified at the strategic command level, HexaForce can propose different courses of action, including firing options using air or land forces, according to Moreau. The operator can then choose a course of action, with the system sending the targeting mission to the tactical level.

“Of course it remains up to the operator to choose to push the button, and to choose the best option proposed by HexaForce,” Moreau said. “There is no automated action.”

In addition to connecting to systems that provide tactical awareness, Hexaforce could include commercial ship-tracking data or cyber threats to provide a more complete picture, Moreau said.

While developed with input from the French Army, the executive repeatedly stressed that the Thales system is designed as a NATO solution rather than a France-specific system. Asked how it compares with existing systems such as Systematic’s SitaWare or Airbus’s Multi-Domain Combat Cloud, Moreau instead focused on the interoperability of the Thales system.

Moreau said HexaForce is ready and already in the hands of the armed forces, with the first version taking nine months from design to making it available to the French Army.

France is developing its sovereign C2 system Arcadia, and Moreau said that while Hexaforce could be “a cornerstone” of the French system, the decision is not up to Thales.

Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.
zhParas: 巴黎——法国国防科技公司泰雷兹（Thales）负责多域作战的副总裁帕特里克·莫罗（Patrick Moreau）表示，该公司正就使用其人工智能驱动的指挥控制系统HexaForce，与多个北约国家进行“相当深入”的讨论。
泰雷兹上周宣布HexaForce已可供使用。此前，该系统于6月在波兰举行的北约“联盟战士互操作性演习”（CWIX）期间进行了测试。该公司将该系统定位为一种多域C2“覆盖层”，可从战略到战术层面接入遗留系统和各国系统，同时允许用户选择自己的人工智能模型，避免供应商锁定。
北约正越来越多地借助人工智能来利用指挥控制中不断增长的数据量，并且已经在运行一套由总部位于美国的Palantir Technologies提供的C2系统。与此同时，欧盟正寻求加快欧洲能力的开发和部署，原因是担心对支撑这些能力的技术的主权控制问题。
“我不想说得太详细，但到目前为止，我们与一些北约国家的某些讨论已经相当深入，”莫罗在9月24日接受《防务新闻》（Defense News）采访时表示。
莫罗表示，随着欧洲和北约军队寻求将行动规模从旅级编队扩大到兵力超过10万人的军级单位，人工智能将成为处理更复杂数据、缩短规划周期和提高态势感知能力的关键。
这位高管表示，HexaForce旨在提供从军级到营级的指挥控制。泰雷兹与最终用户确定了一个目标，即能够每天规划1000个目标打击任务，相当于提高十倍。
莫罗表示，该系统采用围绕北约标准构建的开放架构，使各国能够接入现有系统以执行任务规划等任务，或使用其自行选择的大语言模型。除了大语言模型组件外，HexaForce还包含用于目标打击任务准备等任务的智能体式人工智能。
莫罗表示，该系统采用完全分布式架构，旨在依靠网状能力，使系统能够分布在不同指挥所内的不同数据中枢上，符合不依赖集中式计算的新作战概念。
据莫罗（Moreau）称，通过与遗留解决方案对接，HexaForce 可为武装部队已在使用的系统增添“AI 驱动能力”。他说，HexaForce 是一个指挥控制系统，用户仍需专用战术系统来提供传感器数据。
这位高管表示，在 CWIX 上的目标是让最终用户测试 HexaForce 及其与现有和遗留系统的互操作性。他说，该系统落实了北约与以数据为中心的安全和联邦任务网络框架相关的标准。
莫罗称，对于在战略指挥层识别出的威胁，HexaForce 可以提出不同的行动方案，包括使用空中或地面部队的火力选项。随后，操作员可以选择一种行动方案，系统会将目标打击任务发送至战术层。
“当然，是否按下按钮以及是否选择 HexaForce 提出的最佳方案，仍由操作员决定，”莫罗说，“没有自动化行动。”
莫罗说，除连接提供战术态势感知的系统外，HexaForce 还可纳入商业船舶跟踪数据或网络威胁，以提供更完整的态势图。
尽管该系统在开发过程中吸纳了法国陆军的意见，但这位高管反复强调，泰雷兹系统是按北约解决方案设计的，而非法国专用系统。当被问及与 Systematic 的 SitaWare 或空客的 Multi-Domain Combat Cloud 等现有系统相比如何时，莫罗反而着重谈到泰雷兹系统的互操作性。
莫罗说，HexaForce 已准备就绪，并已交付武装部队使用；首个版本从设计到提供给法国陆军耗时九个月。
法国正在开发其主权 C2 系统 Arcadia，莫罗表示，尽管 HexaForce 可能成为该法国系统的“基石”，但决定权不在泰雷兹。
鲁迪·鲁滕贝格（Rudy Ruitenberg）是《防务新闻》驻欧洲记者。他的职业生涯始于彭博新闻社，在技术、大宗商品市场和政治报道方面拥有丰富经验。

巴黎——法国国防科技公司泰雷兹（Thales）负责多域作战的副总裁帕特里克·莫罗（Patrick Moreau）表示，该公司正就使用其人工智能驱动的指挥控制系统HexaForce，与多个北约国家进行“相当深入”的讨论。

泰雷兹上周宣布HexaForce已可供使用。此前，该系统于6月在波兰举行的北约“联盟战士互操作性演习”（CWIX）期间进行了测试。该公司将该系统定位为一种多域C2“覆盖层”，可从战略到战术层面接入遗留系统和各国系统，同时允许用户选择自己的人工智能模型，避免供应商锁定。

北约正越来越多地借助人工智能来利用指挥控制中不断增长的数据量，并且已经在运行一套由总部位于美国的Palantir Technologies提供的C2系统。与此同时，欧盟正寻求加快欧洲能力的开发和部署，原因是担心对支撑这些能力的技术的主权控制问题。

“我不想说得太详细，但到目前为止，我们与一些北约国家的某些讨论已经相当深入，”莫罗在9月24日接受《防务新闻》（Defense News）采访时表示。

莫罗表示，随着欧洲和北约军队寻求将行动规模从旅级编队扩大到兵力超过10万人的军级单位，人工智能将成为处理更复杂数据、缩短规划周期和提高态势感知能力的关键。

这位高管表示，HexaForce旨在提供从军级到营级的指挥控制。泰雷兹与最终用户确定了一个目标，即能够每天规划1000个目标打击任务，相当于提高十倍。

莫罗表示，该系统采用围绕北约标准构建的开放架构，使各国能够接入现有系统以执行任务规划等任务，或使用其自行选择的大语言模型。除了大语言模型组件外，HexaForce还包含用于目标打击任务准备等任务的智能体式人工智能。

莫罗表示，该系统采用完全分布式架构，旨在依靠网状能力，使系统能够分布在不同指挥所内的不同数据中枢上，符合不依赖集中式计算的新作战概念。

据莫罗（Moreau）称，通过与遗留解决方案对接，HexaForce 可为武装部队已在使用的系统增添“AI 驱动能力”。他说，HexaForce 是一个指挥控制系统，用户仍需专用战术系统来提供传感器数据。

这位高管表示，在 CWIX 上的目标是让最终用户测试 HexaForce 及其与现有和遗留系统的互操作性。他说，该系统落实了北约与以数据为中心的安全和联邦任务网络框架相关的标准。

莫罗称，对于在战略指挥层识别出的威胁，HexaForce 可以提出不同的行动方案，包括使用空中或地面部队的火力选项。随后，操作员可以选择一种行动方案，系统会将目标打击任务发送至战术层。

“当然，是否按下按钮以及是否选择 HexaForce 提出的最佳方案，仍由操作员决定，”莫罗说，“没有自动化行动。”

莫罗说，除连接提供战术态势感知的系统外，HexaForce 还可纳入商业船舶跟踪数据或网络威胁，以提供更完整的态势图。

尽管该系统在开发过程中吸纳了法国陆军的意见，但这位高管反复强调，泰雷兹系统是按北约解决方案设计的，而非法国专用系统。当被问及与 Systematic 的 SitaWare 或空客的 Multi-Domain Combat Cloud 等现有系统相比如何时，莫罗反而着重谈到泰雷兹系统的互操作性。

莫罗说，HexaForce 已准备就绪，并已交付武装部队使用；首个版本从设计到提供给法国陆军耗时九个月。

法国正在开发其主权 C2 系统 Arcadia，莫罗表示，尽管 HexaForce 可能成为该法国系统的“基石”，但决定权不在泰雷兹。

items.title: Desolate Arctic outpost likely to host US troops under new Greenland deal
items.author: Stine Jacobsen, Jacob Gronholt-Pedersen and Tom Little, Reuters
items.summary: Under a U.S. agreement signed this week, a small outpost at Mestersvig, Greenland, could soon become a key American military foothold in the Arctic.
items.body:
At a windswept gravel airstrip in eastern Greenland, a small Danish military detachment has quietly kept watch for decades.

Now, under a new U.S. defense agreement signed this week, the outpost at Mestersvig could soon become a key American military foothold in the Arctic.

Mestersvig sits 149 miles from the nearest settlement (population 330), at the edge of an uninhabited national park larger than Germany and France combined. The place is covered in darkness during winter, with average temperatures of around 14 degrees Fahrenheit.

“This is as remote, as cold, and as extreme as you can find in the world. You have to go to Antarctica to find similar conditions,” said Anders Ibsen, a former officer with Denmark’s Sirius dog sled patrol, an elite unit that uses Mestersvig to resupply.

It oversees the stretch of ocean between Greenland, Iceland and Britain — known as the GIUK gap — that Russia’s Northern Fleet must cross to reach the Atlantic. For NATO, controlling this chokepoint is critical to containing Russian naval power.

Local member of parliament Justus Hansen welcomed the expansion, saying, “In east Greenland, we really need that new money.”

Under the defense agreement, Washington will be allowed to establish a new base at Mestersvig and Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland, potentially marking the first U.S. military expansion on the vast, semi-autonomous Arctic island in decades.

Currently, only three soldiers maintain the facility, which was built in the 1960s and includes barracks to house 150 soldiers.

The U.S. has made no public announcement about its plans for the base.

A HISTORY OF OUTSIDE INTEREST

During World War II, this stretch of the Arctic island’s coast became a front line in the “weather war,” a race between Germany and the Allies to read Greenland’s weather, which shaped conditions over the North Atlantic and Europe days later.

Germany secretly built manned stations here, but Danish dog sled patrols tracked them down, and Allied forces drove them out.

Nearby, an EU-backed project aims to mine molybdenum — a critical metal for aerospace and defence — some 12 miles away. A Texas oil company plans to drill for oil this winter at an untested basin just south of Mestersvig, although it still lacks a permit to do so.

The previous owner, ARCO, spent heavily on seismic work in the 1970s but never drilled.

“Any infrastructural improvements in Greenland would be very welcome,” said Robert Price, CEO of Greenland Energy, the oil company.

The 1.1-mile airstrip — long enough for military transport planes to land — can collect up to 5 meters of snow a year.

“When it’s snowing, you’re basically removing snow 24/7,” said Ibsen, the former dog sled patrol officer who spent a year at Mestersvig.

“You have plenty to do just staying alive.”
zhParas: 在格陵兰东部一条寒风劲吹的砾石简易机场，一支丹麦小规模军事分遣队数十年来一直默默守望。
如今，根据本周签署的一项新美国防务协议，梅斯特斯维格前哨站可能很快成为美国在北极的重要军事立足点。
梅斯特斯维格距最近定居点（人口330）149 miles，位于一座面积超过德国和法国之和的无人国家公园边缘。冬季这里一片漆黑，平均气温约为14 degrees Fahrenheit。
“这里是世界上你能找到的最偏远、最寒冷、最极端的地方。要找到类似条件，你得去南极洲，”丹麦“天狼星”狗拉雪橇巡逻队前军官安德斯·易卜生（Anders Ibsen）说。这支部队是一支精锐单位，利用梅斯特斯维格进行补给。
该前哨站监控着格陵兰、冰岛和英国之间的海域——即GIUK缺口——俄罗斯北方舰队必须穿越该海域才能抵达大西洋。对北约而言，控制这一咽喉要道对于遏制俄罗斯海军力量至关重要。
当地议员尤斯图斯·汉森（Justus Hansen）对扩建表示欢迎，他说：“在格陵兰东部，我们确实需要这笔新资金。”
根据这项防务协议，华盛顿将被允许在梅斯特斯维格以及格陵兰南部的纳萨尔苏瓦克建立新基地，这可能标志着美国数十年来首次在这个广袤、半自治的北极岛屿上扩展军事存在。
目前，只有三名士兵维护该设施；该设施建于20世纪60年代，包括可容纳150名士兵的营房。
美国尚未公开宣布其对该基地的计划。
外部利益介入的历史
二战期间，这座北极岛屿的这段海岸线成为“气象战”的前线——德国与盟国竞相解读格陵兰的天气，而这里的天气会在数日后左右北大西洋和欧洲的气象状况。
德国曾在此秘密修建有人驻守的站点，但丹麦的狗拉雪橇巡逻队追踪到这些站点，盟军将其驱逐。
在附近，一个由欧盟支持的项目计划在大约12英里外开采钼——一种航空航天和国防领域的关键金属。一家得克萨斯石油公司计划今年冬天在 Mestersvig 正南方一个未经勘探的盆地钻探石油，尽管该公司尚未获得相应许可。
此前的所有者 ARCO 公司在20世纪70年代投入巨资进行地震勘探，但从未钻探。
“格陵兰的任何基础设施改善都会非常受欢迎，”石油公司 Greenland Energy 首席执行官罗伯特·普赖斯（Robert Price）说。
这条1.1英里长的简易跑道——足以供军用运输机降落——每年积雪可达5米。
“下雪的时候，你基本上一天到晚都在清雪，”曾在梅斯特斯维格待过一年的前狗拉雪橇巡逻队军官伊布森（Ibsen）说。
“光是活下去，你就有很多事要做。”

在格陵兰东部一条寒风劲吹的砾石简易机场，一支丹麦小规模军事分遣队数十年来一直默默守望。

如今，根据本周签署的一项新美国防务协议，梅斯特斯维格前哨站可能很快成为美国在北极的重要军事立足点。

梅斯特斯维格距最近定居点（人口330）149 miles，位于一座面积超过德国和法国之和的无人国家公园边缘。冬季这里一片漆黑，平均气温约为14 degrees Fahrenheit。

“这里是世界上你能找到的最偏远、最寒冷、最极端的地方。要找到类似条件，你得去南极洲，”丹麦“天狼星”狗拉雪橇巡逻队前军官安德斯·易卜生（Anders Ibsen）说。这支部队是一支精锐单位，利用梅斯特斯维格进行补给。

该前哨站监控着格陵兰、冰岛和英国之间的海域——即GIUK缺口——俄罗斯北方舰队必须穿越该海域才能抵达大西洋。对北约而言，控制这一咽喉要道对于遏制俄罗斯海军力量至关重要。

items.title: AF Week in Photos
items.author: Pentagon News
items.summary: This week's photos feature Airmen from around the globe involved in activities supporting expeditionary operations and defending America. This weekly feature showcases the men and women of the Air Force.
items.body:
POW/MIA Remembrance Week Senior Airman Joseph Drewitz, an MQ-9 Reaper aircraft journeyman assigned to the 25th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron, participates in a ruck march at Nellis Air Force Base, Nev., Sept. 17, 2026. Participants completed events throughout POW/MIA Remembrance Week to honor the service and sacrifice of the nation’s prisoners of war and those who remain missing in action. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Isabella Borrillo)

POW/MIA Remembrance Week

Senior Airman Joseph Drewitz, an MQ-9 Reaper aircraft journeyman assigned to the 25th Aircraft Maintenance Squadron, participates in a ruck march at Nellis Air Force Base, Nev., Sept. 17, 2026. Participants completed events throughout POW/MIA Remembrance Week to honor the service and sacrifice of the nation’s prisoners of war and those who remain missing in action. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Isabella Borrillo)

Northern formation U.S. Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcons and a KC-135 Stratotanker fly in formation while conducting aerial refueling during Operation Arctic Vanguard over Greenland, Sept. 16, 2026. The joint and multinational operation enhances interoperability, tests cold-weather combat readiness and strengthens coalition capabilities across the Arctic region. (U.S. Air Force photo by Maj. David Brown)

U.S. Air Force F-16 Fighting Falcons and a KC-135 Stratotanker fly in formation while conducting aerial refueling during Operation Arctic Vanguard over Greenland, Sept. 16, 2026. The joint and multinational operation enhances interoperability, tests cold-weather combat readiness and strengthens coalition capabilities across the Arctic region. (U.S. Air Force photo by Maj. David Brown)

Cleared for takeoff Air Force running back Rocco Conti hurdles over a defender during a game against Duquesne University at the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colo., Sept. 5, 2026. Air Force shut out Duquesne 34-0 in its season opener. (U.S. Air Force photo by Jonathan Suni)

Cleared for takeoff

Air Force running back Rocco Conti hurdles over a defender during a game against Duquesne University at the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colo., Sept. 5, 2026. Air Force shut out Duquesne 34-0 in its season opener. (U.S. Air Force photo by Jonathan Suni)

Honor flight A U.S. Air Force F-35A Lightning II assigned to the 48th Fighter Wing flies a pattern before a ceremonial flyover at RAF Mildenhall, United Kingdom, Sept. 11, 2026. The formation flew over a 9/11 remembrance ceremony during the U.S. national anthem. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Cody J. A. Mott)

A U.S. Air Force F-35A Lightning II assigned to the 48th Fighter Wing flies a pattern before a ceremonial flyover at RAF Mildenhall, United Kingdom, Sept. 11, 2026. The formation flew over a 9/11 remembrance ceremony during the U.S. national anthem. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Cody J. A. Mott)

Leader of the pack Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David R. Wolfe conducts a question-and-answer session during the 2026 Air, Space and Cyber Conference at National Harbor, Md., Sept. 14, 2026. Wolfe emphasized team-driven combat readiness and the need to prepare adaptable Airmen to operate effectively amid uncertainty. (U.S. Air Force photo by Andy Morataya)

Leader of the pack

Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David R. Wolfe conducts a question-and-answer session during the 2026 Air, Space and Cyber Conference at National Harbor, Md., Sept. 14, 2026. Wolfe emphasized team-driven combat readiness and the need to prepare adaptable Airmen to operate effectively amid uncertainty. (U.S. Air Force photo by Andy Morataya)

Buddy lift Airmen conduct hoist operations from a CV-22 Osprey during a demonstration at Kirtland Air Force Base, N.M., Sept. 14, 2026. The flight was part of a two-day celebration commemorating 20 years of CV-22 aircrew training at Kirtland AFB. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Maurice Casilla)

Airmen conduct hoist operations from a CV-22 Osprey during a demonstration at Kirtland Air Force Base, N.M., Sept. 14, 2026. The flight was part of a two-day celebration commemorating 20 years of CV-22 aircrew training at Kirtland AFB. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman Maurice Casilla)

Preparing for takeoff Capt. Logan Baldwin, a 20th Bomb Squadron pilot, prepares for takeoff aboard a B-52H Stratofortress at Barksdale Air Force Base, La., Aug. 30, 2026. Bomber Task Force missions enable crews to maintain a high state of readiness and proficiency while validating the Air Force’s always-ready global strike capability. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Rhea Beil)

Preparing for takeoff

Capt. Logan Baldwin, a 20th Bomb Squadron pilot, prepares for takeoff aboard a B-52H Stratofortress at Barksdale Air Force Base, La., Aug. 30, 2026. Bomber Task Force missions enable crews to maintain a high state of readiness and proficiency while validating the Air Force’s always-ready global strike capability. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Rhea Beil)

Two of a kind Two F-15E Strike Eagles assigned to the 4th Fighter Wing emerge through clouds over North Carolina, Sept. 12, 2026. The aircraft flew in tandem with a KC-46A Pegasus assigned to the 916th Air Refueling Wing during aerial refueling operations that also supported a flyover at NC Freedom Fest in Goldsboro, N.C. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Hudson Steiner)

Two of a kind

Two F-15E Strike Eagles assigned to the 4th Fighter Wing emerge through clouds over North Carolina, Sept. 12, 2026. The aircraft flew in tandem with a KC-46A Pegasus assigned to the 916th Air Refueling Wing during aerial refueling operations that also supported a flyover at NC Freedom Fest in Goldsboro, N.C. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Hudson Steiner)

Lighting the way A U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command loadmaster holds an LUU-2C/B illuminating flare aboard an MC-130J Commando II during airdrop training off the coast of Okinawa, Japan, Sept. 9, 2026. During the training, loadmasters released the flares to provide target training for F-22 Raptor weapons systems. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Melany Bermudez)

Lighting the way

A U.S. Air Force Special Operations Command loadmaster holds an LUU-2C/B illuminating flare aboard an MC-130J Commando II during airdrop training off the coast of Okinawa, Japan, Sept. 9, 2026. During the training, loadmasters released the flares to provide target training for F-22 Raptor weapons systems. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Melany Bermudez)

Fueling the fight A B-52H Stratofortress assigned to the 5th Bomb Wing, Minot Air Force Base, N.D., receives fuel from a KC-135 Stratotanker assigned to the 185th Air Refueling Wing, Iowa Air National Guard, over South Dakota, Sept. 15, 2026. The 185th ARW aircrew conducted the impromptu refueling after completing a separate aerial refueling mission with a B-1B Lancer in the area. (U.S. Air Force photo by Staff Sgt. John Johnson)

Fueling the fight

A B-52H Stratofortress assigned to the 5th Bomb Wing, Minot Air Force Base, N.D., receives fuel from a KC-135 Stratotanker assigned to the 185th Air Refueling Wing, Iowa Air National Guard, over South Dakota, Sept. 15, 2026. The 185th ARW aircrew conducted the impromptu refueling after completing a separate aerial refueling mission with a B-1B Lancer in the area. (U.S. Air Force photo by Staff Sgt. John Johnson)

Simulation evacuation Maj. Paul Pikman, a Critical Care Air Transport Team physician, and Maj. Owen Caron, a CCATT registered nurse, perform a simulated patient medical evacuation during exercise Ultimate Caduceus 2026 at Scott Air Force Base, Ill., Sept. 8, 2026. After receiving the simulated patient, the medical professionals conducted a medical assessment before transferring the patient to another aircraft for transport. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Izcalli X. Martinez)

Maj. Paul Pikman, a Critical Care Air Transport Team physician, and Maj. Owen Caron, a CCATT registered nurse, perform a simulated patient medical evacuation during exercise Ultimate Caduceus 2026 at Scott Air Force Base, Ill., Sept. 8, 2026. After receiving the simulated patient, the medical professionals conducted a medical assessment before transferring the patient to another aircraft for transport. (U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Izcalli X. Martinez)

No runway required A U.S. Air Force C-130J Super Hercules assigned to the 37th Airlift Squadron operates from a sand landing zone in Rømø, Denmark, during exercise Northern Viking 26, Aug. 25, 2026. Operating from varied surfaces reduces reliance on established airfields and gives commanders additional options to disperse, position and sustain forces. (U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Edgar Grimaldo)

No runway required

A U.S. Air Force C-130J Super Hercules assigned to the 37th Airlift Squadron operates from a sand landing zone in Rømø, Denmark, during exercise Northern Viking 26, Aug. 25, 2026. items.title: Air Force, Pentagon Work to Boost Military Spouse Employment
items.author: Greg Hadley
items.summary: New Air Force, Pentagon, and White House initiatives aim to chip away at an issue that has long frustrated leaders and families across the military: spouse employment. For years now, the percentage of unemployed military spouses has held steady at around 20 percent, experts say. The post Air Force, Pentagon Work to Boost Military Spouse Employment appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .
items.body:
New Air Force, Pentagon, and White House initiatives are taking a new swing at an issue that has long frustrated military families: barriers to spouse employment.

Unemployment and underemployment have plagued military spouses for years, with the unemployment rate among military spouses holding steady at around 20 percent—despite initiatives to promote spouse preferences for hiring on base, support for remote work, and advocacy for making professional licenses more portable across state borders.

Improving spouses employment is not a “charitable initiative,” but a major retention and readiness incentive, argued Lyndsey Akers, a consultant with AFA’s United Forces & Families program.

“When military spouses have greater access to meaningful and sustainable careers, we strengthen the economic stability of military families,” Akers said at AFA’s Air, Space & Cyber conference last week. “We support the conditions that enable continued service, and we connect employers with an experienced, adaptable, and often overlooked talent pool.”

Top-down interest from the White House’s new Military Spouse Commission is driving renewed interest in the topic.

Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Military Community and Family Policy Stephen Simmons said at the conference that the nation “has admired” the problem for too long; but “we haven’t done enough about it, and to get an issue the attention it needs, usually, first off, you have to elevate.”

Cindy Wilsbach, wife of Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Kenneth S. Wilsbach and a senior writer for presidential correspondence at the White House employee, said the new commission President Donald Trump’s interest.

“It was marching orders from the leader of the free world to say, ‘We see the military spouse family and we recognize there are some longstanding generational problems that we need to get after,’” Cindy Wilsbach said during a panel discussion.

Both Wilsbachs are members of the commission, as are all the service chiefs, their spouses, and their senior enlisted advisors, and their spouses, including:

- Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas A. Schiess and his wife Debbie Schiess

- Chief Master Sergeant of the Air Force David Wolfe and his wife, Dr. Doniel Wolfe

- Chief Master Sergeant of the Space Force John F. Bentivegna and his wife Cathy Bentivegna

“With the four spouses here going to be involved with the Military Spouse Commission, we’ve got an opportunity to make some real change to laws that prevent us from hiring people fast enough and putting people into jobs and places and moving positions around,” said CMSAF David Wolfe during a panel discussion.

Cindy Wilsbach said the commission won’t try to reinvent efforts already underway but instead “will add to the work that’s being done,” while raising the profile of the issue to give advocates access to the President and other high-level decision-makers.

Global Military Spouse Connection

One program that’s newly in place and starting to grow is the Air Force’s Global Military Spouse Connection, which started in June as a pilot program for just a few installations.

Officials say the program is meant to serve as a “bridge” between Active-Duty military spouses who have PCSed to a new location and local hiring managers.

“Using career field administrators, GMSC creates a structured, active pipeline to connect the military spouse talent pool with employment opportunities,” according to an Air Force release.

“We are assisting hiring managers in finding the best-qualified individual,” said career field administrator Wyteeshia McRoberts, in a statement. “We’re not contacting them to do favors. We are looking at resumes, seeing what they qualify for and making recommendations for the right jobs.”

CMSAF Wolfe highlighted the program in his Sept. 14 keynote address to the conference, noting how the program “went from idea to first action in only 60 days,” and promising rapid expansion. On Sept. 22, the Air Force announced the program was already available for spouses moving to the following locations:

- Luke Air Force Base, Ariz.

- Goodfellow Air Force Base, Texas

- Laughlin Air Force Base, Texas

- Mountain Home Air Force Base, Idaho

- Travis Air Force Base, Calif.

- Patrick Space Force Base, Fla.

- Ramstein Air Base, Germany

- RAF Croughton, U.K.

- RAF Mildenhall, U.K.

- RAF Lakenheath, U.K.

- RAF Feltwell, U.K.

- Kadena Air Base, Japan

While the Department of the Air Force has launched the new connection program, the Office of the Secretary of Defense is focused on better publicizing the programs it already has, said Simmons.

Until recently, spouses looking for Pentagon help to land jobs, scholarships, or fellowships were on their own navigating a confusing sea of acronyms: SECO, MyCAA, MSEP.

SECO stood for Spouse Education and Career Opportunities, but wasn’t visible enough to leaders or community members, Simmons said. So his team rebranded to “SpouseWorks” and changed the organization. Before, the program “was buried in one of our directorships through no fault of their own,” Simmons said. “But in my mind, … it needed to report directly to me, so we turned it from a sub-office to a directorship.”

Other programs were folded in, so that now there are also SpouseWorks Fellowship and SpouseWorks Scholarship programs. “We’re trying to make it very simple and easy to use.”

SpouseWorks offers training, education, and professional development; career coaches; and a job board. Simmons said the goal is to be a one-stop shop for military spouses and a resource for employers seeking high-quality employees.

Early returns are promising. “We’re up well over 50 to 80 percent usage year over year,” he said. “And we’re only about halfway through the first year of the SpouseWorks rebrand.”

Headwinds continue, however. “I wish we could say that we had a lot of consistency, but what happens is with every change of leadership, somebody has a bright idea and then a great program goes away,” said Sue Luangkhot Hoppin, president of the National Military Spouse Network. “We don’t dot the Is and cross the Ts and we don’t necessarily solidify the programs before we move on to the next one.”

Lack of consistency from base to base, due to different commanders’ priorities, is also a challenge, he said. Elevating the issue to department leaders can raise the profile and relieve operational commanders of an extra burden.

One policy change that had unintended consequences for families was the widespread rollback of remote work options for federal civilians. Because of frequent PCS moves, remote work is an ideal option for many military spouses. “Remote work is a lifeline for a lot of military spouses,” Luangkhot Hoppin said. “It allows them to work even if they have childcare issues. But if they have to go back to the office, all of a sudden they need to have access to affordable child care, and that’s become an issue.”

Liz O’Brien, senior vice president at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation, argued that remote work is only a piece of the equation, noting that during the COVID-19 pandemic, when remote work options surged, spouse unemployment stayed stubbornly high. Childcare is one of the biggest barriers to better spouse employment, O’Brien, Luangkhot Hoppin, and Simmons agreed. Simmons sees an “intrinsic relationship” between the two; without ready and available childcare, many spouses can’t work. If they have to wait months for childcare openings to materialize, their window for employment can begin to close down.

Simmons said the Pentagon is working multiple fronts to reduce the wait times for childcare, both through expanded capacity at its Child Development Centers as well as through partnerships with the Armed Forces YMCA, private industry, and support for informal childcare support.

“Year over year … our childcare wait lists are down 25 percent, which is phenomenal,” Simmons said. And the tie to spouse employment is clear. “As a result, you see that wait list drop, you also see the spouse employment drop.”
zhParas: 空军、五角大楼和白宫推出的新举措，正对一个长期令军人家庭深感困扰的问题发起新一轮冲击：军人配偶的就业障碍。
多年来，失业与就业不足一直困扰着军人配偶，军人配偶的失业率始终徘徊在20%左右——尽管已有多项举措出台，包括在基地招聘中给予军人配偶优先照顾、支持远程办公，以及推动职业执照在跨州之间更易通用。
空军协会（AFA）“联合部队与家庭”项目顾问林赛·阿克斯（Lyndsey Akers）认为，改善军人配偶就业并非一项“慈善举措”，而是一项重大的留任与战备激励措施。
“当军人配偶有更多机会获得有意义且可持续的职业时，我们就能增强军人家庭的经济稳定性，”阿克斯上周在空军协会“航空、航天与网络”会议上说。“我们为有利于持续服役的条件提供支持，并把雇主与一个经验丰富、适应力强且往往被忽视的人才库连接起来。”
白宫新设立的军人配偶委员会自上而下的关注，正推动这一议题重新受到重视。
负责军事社区与家庭政策的国防部副助理部长斯蒂芬·西蒙斯（Stephen Simmons）在会上表示，美国对这个问题的“赞赏”已经太久了；但“我们做得还不够，而要让一个问题获得应有的关注，通常首先必须把它提升到更高层级。”
空军参谋长肯尼思·S·威尔巴赫（Kenneth S. Wilsbach）上将的妻子、白宫总统通信高级撰稿人辛迪·威尔巴赫（Cindy Wilsbach）表示，这个新委员会体现了总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）的兴趣所在。
“这是自由世界的领袖下达的明确指令：‘我们看到了军人配偶家庭，也认识到存在一些长期积累、代际相传的问题，需要我们着手解决，’”辛迪·威尔巴赫在一次小组讨论中说。
威尔巴赫（Wilsbach）夫妇二人都是该委员会成员，所有军种首长及其配偶，以及他们的高级士兵顾问及其配偶也都是委员会成员，包括：
- 太空作战部长 Gen. 道格拉斯·A·希斯（Douglas A. Schiess）及其妻子黛比·希斯（Debbie Schiess）
- 美国空军首席军士长戴维·沃尔夫（David Wolfe）及其妻子多尼尔·沃尔夫博士（Dr. Doniel Wolfe）
- 美国太空军首席军士长约翰·F·本蒂韦尼亚（John F. Bentivegna）及其妻子凯茜·本蒂韦尼亚（Cathy Bentivegna）
“随着这里的四位配偶即将参与军人配偶委员会，我们有机会对法律作出真正的改变；这些法律阻碍我们足够快地招聘人员、把人员安排到岗位和地点，以及调动职位，”CMSAF 戴维·沃尔夫在一次小组讨论中表示。
辛迪·威尔巴赫（Cindy Wilsbach）表示，该委员会不会试图另起炉灶重做已经在进行的工作，而是“将为正在开展的工作添砖加瓦”，同时提高这一议题的关注度，让倡导者能够接触总统和其他高层决策者。
全球军人配偶联系
一项新近落地并开始发展壮大的计划，是空军的“全球军人配偶联系”；该计划于 6 月作为试点项目启动，最初仅面向少数基地。
官员表示，该计划旨在充当已PCS调动至新地点的现役军人配偶与当地招聘经理之间的“桥梁”。
据空军发布的消息，“GMSC利用职业领域管理员，打造了一条结构化、活跃的输送通道，将军人配偶人才库与就业机会连接起来。”
“我们正在帮助招聘经理找到最符合资格的人选，”职业领域管理员怀蒂希娅·麦克罗伯茨（Wyteeshia McRoberts）在一份声明中说。“我们联系他们并非为了托人情。我们是在审阅简历，了解他们符合哪些岗位条件，并为合适的职位提出推荐。”
CMSAF沃尔夫（Wolfe）在9月14日向会议发表的主旨演讲中强调了该计划，指出该计划“从构想变为首次行动仅用了60天”，并承诺迅速扩大。9月22日，空军宣布该计划已面向迁往以下地点的配偶开放：
- 卢克空军基地，亚利桑那州
- 古德费洛空军基地，得克萨斯州
- 劳克林空军基地，得克萨斯州
- 芒廷霍姆空军基地，爱达荷州
特拉维斯空军基地，加利福尼亚州
帕特里克太空军基地，佛罗里达州
拉姆施泰因空军基地，德国
英国皇家空军克劳顿基地，英国
英国皇家空军米尔登霍尔基地，英国
英国皇家空军莱肯希思基地，英国
英国皇家空军费尔特韦尔基地，英国
嘉手纳空军基地，日本
西蒙斯（Simmons）表示，虽然空军部已经启动了新的联系计划，但国防部长办公室的重点是更好地宣传其已有的项目。
直到最近，寻求五角大楼帮助以找到工作、获得奖学金或研究金的军人配偶，还只能独自在令人困惑的缩写海洋中摸索：SECO、MyCAA、MSEP。
西蒙斯说，SECO 原本代表配偶教育与职业机会，但对领导层或社区成员来说知名度不够。因此，他的团队将其更名为“SpouseWorks”，并改变了组织架构。西蒙斯说，此前该计划“被埋没在我们某个主任办公室之下，这不是他们自己的过错”。“但在我看来，……它需要直接向我汇报，所以我们把它从一个下属办公室提升为一个主任办公室。”
其他计划也被并入，因此现在还有 SpouseWorks Fellowship 和 SpouseWorks Scholarship 项目。“我们正努力让它变得非常简单、易于使用。”
SpouseWorks 提供培训、教育和职业发展；职业教练；以及一个招聘信息板。西蒙斯说，目标是成为军人配偶的一站式服务机构，并成为寻求高素质员工的雇主的资源。
初步结果令人鼓舞。“我们的使用量同比增长远超50%至80%，”他说。“而 SpouseWorks 更名后的第一年才刚过去大约一半。”
然而，阻力依然存在。“我希望我们能说我们有很多一致性，但现实是，每逢领导层更替，就会有人灵光一现，然后一个很好的项目就消失了，”全国军人配偶网络主席苏·卢昂科特·霍平（Sue Luangkhot Hoppin）说。“我们做事不够严谨，也不一定在转向下一个项目之前把现有项目巩固好。”
他说，由于不同指挥官的优先事项不同，各基地之间缺乏一致性也是一个挑战。将这一问题提升到部门领导层，可以提高其关注度，并减轻作战指挥官的额外负担。
一项给军人家庭带来意外后果的政策变化，是联邦文职人员远程办公选项被大范围取消。由于频繁的PCS调动，远程办公对许多军人配偶来说是理想选择。“远程办公是许多军人配偶的生命线，”卢昂科特·霍平（Luangkhot Hoppin）说。“它让他们即使有托儿问题也能工作。但如果他们必须回办公室，突然间就需要获得负担得起的托儿服务，而这已经成了一个难题。”

美国商会基金会高级副总裁利兹·奥布莱恩（Liz O’Brien）认为，远程办公只是问题的一部分；她指出，在COVID-19疫情期间，远程办公选项激增时，军人配偶失业率仍居高不下。奥布莱恩、卢昂科特·霍平和西蒙斯（Simmons）一致认为，托儿是改善军人配偶就业的最大障碍之一。西蒙斯认为两者之间存在“内在联系”；如果没有现成可用的托儿服务，许多配偶就无法工作。如果他们必须等上几个月才能等到托儿名额出现，他们的就业窗口就可能开始关闭。
西蒙斯说，五角大楼正在多条战线努力缩短托儿等候时间，既通过扩大其儿童发展中心的容量，也通过与武装部队基督教青年会、私营行业合作，并支持非正式托儿服务。
“同比来看……我们的托儿等候名单减少了25%，这非常了不起，”西蒙斯说。而且它与军人配偶就业的联系显而易见。“因此，你会看到等候名单减少，也会看到军人配偶就业下降。”

他说，由于不同指挥官的优先事项不同，各基地之间缺乏一致性也是一个挑战。将这一问题提升到部门领导层，可以提高其关注度，并减轻作战指挥官的额外负担。

一项给军人家庭带来意外后果的政策变化，是联邦文职人员远程办公选项被大范围取消。由于频繁的PCS调动，远程办公对许多军人配偶来说是理想选择。“远程办公是许多军人配偶的生命线，”卢昂科特·霍平（Luangkhot Hoppin）说。“它让他们即使有托儿问题也能工作。但如果他们必须回办公室，突然间就需要获得负担得起的托儿服务，而这已经成了一个难题。”

美国商会基金会高级副总裁利兹·奥布莱恩（Liz O’Brien）认为，远程办公只是问题的一部分；她指出，在COVID-19疫情期间，远程办公选项激增时，军人配偶失业率仍居高不下。奥布莱恩、卢昂科特·霍平和西蒙斯（Simmons）一致认为，托儿是改善军人配偶就业的最大障碍之一。西蒙斯认为两者之间存在“内在联系”；如果没有现成可用的托儿服务，许多配偶就无法工作。如果他们必须等上几个月才能等到托儿名额出现，他们的就业窗口就可能开始关闭。

西蒙斯说，五角大楼正在多条战线努力缩短托儿等候时间，既通过扩大其儿童发展中心的容量，也通过与武装部队基督教青年会、私营行业合作，并支持非正式托儿服务。

“同比来看……我们的托儿等候名单减少了25%，这非常了不起，”西蒙斯说。而且它与军人配偶就业的联系显而易见。“因此，你会看到等候名单减少，也会看到军人配偶就业下降。”

items.title: France to send military to protect Saudi Arabia on Red Sea oil route, Macron says
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: France will send troops and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, Macron said.
items.body:
PARIS, Sept 24 (Reuters) — France will send troops and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday.

Macron also said a U.S. ban on diesel exports, which the White House has denied is under consideration, would be “catastrophic,” both globally and for the U.S. economy.

Macron was speaking in a wide-ranging primetime television interview on the international situation, in which he also warned about possible Russian attacks on French soil.

Facing growing pressure at home over high energy prices, Macron sought to assure the French that France had adequate gas and oil supplies as winter approaches. He said Paris was actively working to ensure flows were not disrupted.

Crude oil prices have surged recently as the main alternative route for Saudi oil exports through Yanbu has come under missile attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

“We are going to send military resources, that is to say, soldiers, radar systems and defense systems, to protect this site — not to get us involved in any conflicts, but to protect this site,” Macron told TF1 and France 2 TV.

Macron dismissed a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo that the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency had warned European governments about the threat of potential drone attacks from the Mediterranean.

“I can deny it. The CIA did not inform French services,” he said.

Still, Macron said Russia is multiplying hostile and criminal acts against European countries, and France could face strikes similar to the failed attack in Leipzig. Germany said Russia was responsible for an attempted drone attack in August on the Leipzig airport.

Macron gathered French party chiefs at the Elysee last week to brief them on the growing threat from Russia. He later said he had ordered his government to draw up a plan to protect critical infrastructure against drone and cyber attacks.

Macron said Moscow was seeking to intimidate Europe and break the continent’s resolve in supporting Ukraine.

Russia says European allegations of hybrid attacks are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria.

Yet Macron’s position on Russia was weakened this week after France shocked other EU members by getting Russian-Uzbek metals tycoon Alisher Usmanov exempted from EU sanctions, citing national security concerns. That prompted Azerbaijan to pardon a French national jailed for espionage.
zhParas: 巴黎，9月24日（路透社）——法国总统马克龙（Emmanuel Macron）周四表示，法国将向沙特阿拉伯派遣部队和防御系统，以帮助保护红海港口城市延布，该地对能源运输至关重要。
马克龙还表示，美国禁止柴油出口——白宫否认正在考虑这一举措——无论对全球还是对美国经济而言都将是“灾难性的”。
马克龙是在一次内容广泛的黄金时段电视采访中就国际形势发表上述言论的，他在采访中还警告称俄罗斯可能对法国本土发动袭击。
面对国内因能源价格高企而日益增大的压力，马克龙试图让法国人放心，随着冬季临近，法国拥有充足的天然气和石油供应。他说，巴黎正在积极努力确保供应不中断。
近期原油价格大幅飙升，原因是沙特石油出口经由延布的主要替代路线遭到也门受伊朗支持的胡塞武装的导弹袭击。
“我们将派遣军事资源，也就是说，士兵、雷达系统和防御系统，来保护这一地点——不是让我们卷入任何冲突，而是为了保护这一地点，”马克龙对TF1和France 2电视台表示。
马克龙否认了西班牙《世界报》（El Mundo）的一篇报道，该报道称美国中央情报局曾就来自地中海的潜在无人机袭击威胁向欧洲各国政府发出警告。
“我可以否认这一点。中情局没有通知法国情报部门，”他说。
尽管如此，马克龙 (Macron) 表示，俄罗斯正在不断增加针对欧洲国家的敌对和犯罪行为，法国可能面临与莱比锡未遂袭击类似的打击。德国表示，俄罗斯应对8月针对莱比锡机场的一起未遂无人机袭击负责。
马克龙上周在爱丽舍宫召集法国各党派领袖，向他们通报来自俄罗斯的日益增长的威胁。他随后表示，已命令政府制定一项计划，保护关键基础设施免受无人机和网络攻击。
马克龙表示，莫斯科正试图恐吓欧洲，并瓦解欧洲大陆支持乌克兰的决心。
俄罗斯表示，欧洲关于混合攻击的指控毫无根据，是反俄歇斯底里的结果。
然而，本周马克龙在俄罗斯问题上的立场遭到削弱，此前法国以国家安全关切为由，使俄罗斯-乌兹别克金属大亨阿利舍尔·乌斯马诺夫 (Alisher Usmanov) 获得欧盟制裁豁免，令其他欧盟成员国感到震惊。这促使阿塞拜疆赦免了一名因间谍罪入狱的法国公民。
